SR5.ActionSourceReplaceClip: Remove and Insert clip / belt / drum
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopBannerFolder_D: Folder of the vendor banners (3:1 images named after the templates, "Armurier-des-ombres-1.webp"…). Empty: the Megapack ones when it is active, else no banner.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopConfig_D: The item compendiums the shop sells, and who may buy.
SR5.SETTINGS_Window_D: Every setting of the system, sorted into tabs (Combat, Magic, Matrix, Shop…). A player sees only their own settings.
SR5.TOKENDEFAULTS_Menu_D: The token given, when they are created, to the spirits, sprites, IC, devices, drones and agents the system creates: size, disposition, bars, displayed name, vision. Left on "—", a field keeps the system's behaviour.
SR5.TOKENDEFAULTS_Intro: For each family, the token given to the actor when it is created (summoning, compiling, IC laid, drone or agent taken out of a sheet…). "—" keeps what the system gives today.
SR5.TOKENDEFAULTS_Hint: Applied at creation only: a token already on the map does not change, and the token kept when a spirit or sprite was dismissed still comes first. Size in squares (0.5 to 10), vision range in scene units, metres on a scene in metres (0 = sees only what is lit, as today).
SR5.RULELOCKS_Menu_D: Where the system refuses an action in the name of a book rule, each family of rules can be lifted: the action goes through, the computations stay, and the GM gets a whisper. By default, the book: everything checked.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Intro: Checked, the system applies the book's rule and refuses the action. Unchecked, it departs from the book: the action goes through anyway, computations and counters do not change, and the GM is told by a whisper (once per character and per combat round).
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_actions_D: Reloading without the action it needs, initiative for an interruption, parry or block without the skill, Edge spent during an extended test (SR5 p. 161-168, 190-191); and the box below, which lifts missing actions only.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_ranges_D: Melee reach, extreme range, number of targets, fanning, frisking at contact, lockpicking from afar.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_ammo_D: Ammunition for the firing mode, reloading in combat, Vintage weapons, accessory capacity.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_magic_D: Blight, ritual circle, shaping beyond Magic, spirit already bound, preparation at Potency 0.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_matrix_D: Resonance, wireless off, marks required, reboot under link-lock, emulation, full PAN, shared vision.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_body_D: Rejected implants, Essence at 0, stun healed first, Better Than Bad healing, medkit.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Family_objects_D: Full storage, Palming for theft and concealment, target already held, drug designer without Chemistry, vehicle mod beyond its slots; and the two boxes below.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Case_missingActions: Block an action the character no longer has: actions per pass and an initiative score of 0 or less (SR5 p. 160-163)
SR5.RULELOCKS_Case_garage: Check the lifestyle behind a garage (Run Faster p. 221)
SR5.RULELOCKS_Case_lockpick: Lockpicking requires a lockpick set (SR5 p. 447)
SR5.RULELOCKS_ShopHint: The shop keeps its own rules (buyers, creation caps, availability) in the Shop tab.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Whisper: {actor}: rule "{family}" lifted, the action went through. Lifted refusal: {message}
SR5.RULELOCKS_NoActionLeftLifted: {actor} had no {action} action left in this pass ({current} left, {value} needed): it is spent anyway.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Ask_Intro: Where a book rule forbids it, the system refuses an action. How should this world play?
SR5.RULELOCKS_Ask_light_D: no refusal: the action goes, the computations stay, and the GM gets a whisper.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Ask_advanced_D: the book: every rule applies, blocking an action one no longer has included.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Ask_custom_D: nothing is applied; the Shadowrun Settings open on the Presets tab, to choose setting by setting.
SR5.RULELOCKS_Ask_Later: Light and Advanced apply the automation preset of that name (Shadowrun Settings → Presets), which can be changed at any time, with the optional rules of the books and the house rules. Closing this window applies "Advanced".
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationLevel_D: Highest Availability and rating of gear bought in Creation mode (SR5 p. 64 and p. 418). "Custom" uses the two values below.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMaxAvailability: Only used when the creation level is "Custom".
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMaxRating_D: Rating or Device Rating. Only used when the creation level is "Custom"; 0 = no limit.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationOverLimit_D: Unchecked (the book, SR5 p. 64 and 418): an item past the Availability or rating allowed at creation is refused. Checked (house rule): it goes in the cart and is bought, marked on the sheet, and the gamemaster sees it in the creation summary.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationOverLimit_T: Shop: at creation, allow what goes past the limits (reported to the gamemaster)
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopGradeGamma_D: Optional rule. Offers gammaware at the counter (Essence ×0.4, Availability +12, cost ×5), never in creation mode.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopGradeGreyware_D: Offers greyware for cyberware only (Essence ×0.75, cost ×1.3), creation included. No wireless. An Awakened character also loses 1 point of Magic (taken automatically) and 1 point of maximum Magic per implant: the shop asks for confirmation before the purchase.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMarketOpen_D: Unticked, players only buy from the GM's vendors (a Grunt carrying a "Shop" storage).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMarketOpen_T: Shop: the market is open to players
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopVendorTest_D: By default an item on the shelf has already been found and is bought without a test (SR5 p. 416: the test is the search). Ticked, the test and the dot come back on the stock.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopVendorTest_T: Shop: availability test at a vendor's too
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritDefaultImages_D: A spirit created, summoned or taken from a compendium gets the portrait and token of its type, sized by its Force: small (1 to 3), medium (4 to 6), large (7 to 9), colossal (10 and more). They follow changes of type and Force. A picture chosen by the gamemaster is never replaced. A custom type takes the pictures of its base type. On by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_IceDefaultImages_D: An IC created or taken from a compendium gets the portrait and token of its type (Acid, Killer, Patrol…). They follow changes of type. A picture chosen by the gamemaster is never replaced. On by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpriteDefaultImages_D: A sprite created, compiled or taken from a compendium gets the portrait and token of its type (Courier, Crack, Data, Fault, Machine, Companion, Generalist), whatever its Level. They follow changes of type. A picture chosen by the gamemaster is never replaced. On by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_ContactDefaultImages_D: A contact called from a character's sheet gets a portrait and the round token made for it: picked by its metatype, its job (the contact's Type field) and its gender when a picture matches, at random otherwise. The same contact always gets the same face. A picture chosen on the contact or by the gamemaster, even one taken from the contacts' bank, is never replaced. On by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritDrainAttribute_D: The book has critters and spirits resist the Drain of an innate spell "with either Intuition or Charisma", at the gamemaster's discretion (SR5 p. 398). The system adds the chosen attribute to Willpower, as a magician's tradition attribute is (Shadow Spells p. 17): a reading, the book does not name Willpower. Spirit sheets only. Charisma by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritDrainAttribute_T: Spirits: attribute resisting the Drain of an innate spell
SR5.SharedVisionShareHint: The checked players see on the map what this device sees, on top of what their own tokens see. Invite Mark is a simple action (SR5 p. 240), counted in combat.
SR5.SharedVisionNoPlayer: No player to share the vision with.
SR5.SharedVisionNoMark: No mark left on {name}: no traffic to intercept (Snoop, SR5 p. 242).
SR5.SharedVisionNoToken: {name} has no token on an active scene: nothing to see through.
SR5.SharedVisionNoPlayerFor: No player owns {name}: nobody to give the vision to.
SR5.CreationActorEnded: {name}: creation over. The shop no longer applies the creation caps.
SR5.CreationActorStarted: {name} is in creation: creation caps at the shop, purchases charged, no Essence hole.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopContactFence_D: Percentage of the listed price a contact pays per point of Loyalty (SR5 p. 419: 5).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopContactFence_T: Fence: share paid by a contact
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopCreationMode_D: Add gear from the shop without charging it. World setting, gamemaster only.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDealerKeywords_D: Comma-separated words. A contact whose type contains one of them gets the +2 Bargaining specialization on availability tests.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDealerKeywords_T: Shop: contact types that deal in goods
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBase_D: What a found buyer starts from, as a percentage of the listed price (SR5 p. 418: 25).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBase_T: Fence: share of the listed price
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceBuyerPool_D: Dice the buyer haggles with. The book gives none, so the table sets it.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceStep_D: How much each net hit of the haggling moves the price, either way (SR5 p. 418: 5).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceThreshold_D: Threshold of the extended Etiquette + Charisma test (SR5 p. 418: 10).
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopFenceThreshold_T: Fence: threshold to find a buyer
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopMaxSurchargeDice_D: Most dice a surcharge can buy (SR5 p. 416: 12, four times the price). 0 removes the cap.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopSurchargePerDie_D: Percentage of the price to offer on top for one extra die on the availability test (SR5 p. 416: 25).
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_flag: Actors whose "Can shop" box is ticked
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_folder: Actors in the folder below (sub-folders included)
SR5.ShopBuyerMode_folderOrFlag: The folder or the "Can shop" box
SR5.ShopCartBlocked: A cart line will not go through the till: hover it to see why.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopDelivery_D: An item with an availability is found after the search time (SR5 p. 418): it is paid when ordered, waits on the sheet under "On order", and the GM delivers it with one click when the world clock reaches its due time. "Immediate" delivers at checkout, as before.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpress_D: Not in the book. The player may tick "Express" when ordering: she pays a surcharge and receives sooner. It is a better deal than the surcharge of the book (SR5 p. 416), on purpose.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpressSurcharge_D: Share of the base price added to a line delivered express.
SR5.SETTINGS_ShopExpressFactor_D: The search time the test gave is divided by this number.
SR5.ShopExpressLabel: Express: +{surcharge}% of the price, time divided by {factor}
SR5.ShopOrderCancelAsked: Cancellation request sent to the GM.
SR5.ShopOrderAwaitsGM: Order placed and paid. No GM is connected: it will be entered in the GM's ledger as soon as one is back.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelText: {user} asks to cancel the order of {actor}: {name}. {price} ¥ will be refunded.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelRefused: The GM refused to cancel the order of {actor}: {name}.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelVendor: The vendor {vendor} pays it back: its cashbox first, its accounts for the rest.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelNoVendor: No vendor in the GM's ledger: only the sheet is refunded.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelNotInLedger: Not in the GM's ledger: no automatic refund. Refund by hand if the order is real.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelDebitGone: The debit of this purchase ({paid} ¥) was deleted or lowered on the sheet: {left} ¥ is left, and the refund stops there.
SR5.ShopOrderCancelActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM cancels an order: they keep the order ledger.
SR5.SocketUseConfirm: {user} asks: {what}. The card comes from their player: the system counted {value} again on its dice, within the sheet's pool, but cannot check the dice themselves. Apply?
SR5.WARN_WoundGroupTreated: {user} asks to heal {patient}, but this group of wounds has been treated already (first aid or the Heal spell once per group, no first aid after Heal; core rulebook p. 206-207). Nothing is applied: new damage opens a new group. If that is the case and the system did not see it, heal by hand.
SR5.SocketUseConfirmRead: {user} asks: {what}. The hold ({value}) is read on their player's card: the system does not count it again on the dice and cannot check it. Apply?
SR5.SocketUseMarks: {name} ({marks} mark(s); hits counted again: the winner's)
SR5.MatrixApiConfirm: {user} asks, through a module: {what}. No card stands behind it. Apply?
SR5.MatrixConvergenceNotConnected: Convergence asked on {name}, who has no active device: out of the Matrix, their persona is not touched (no damage, no reboot, no marks).
SR5.MatrixConvergenceGrid: Convergence on {name}: matrix damage DV {damage} to resist, forced reboot (marks erased, Overwatch Score back to 0, dumpshock in VR).
SR5.MatrixConvergenceLocated: The demigod reports the physical location to the owner of the grid, and to the owner of the host it was in.
SR5.MatrixConvergenceStealth: Sneak was running: the physical location stays unknown (SR5 p. 246).
SR5.MatrixConvergenceHost: Convergence in the host {host}: {name} is neither fried nor ejected. The host puts {marks} marks on the persona and starts launching IC; if it leaves the host, the demigod converges at once (SR5 p. 247).
SR5.MatrixConvergenceHostNoMark: Convergence in the host {host}: {name} is neither fried nor ejected. The host should put {marks} marks on the persona, but none was put: {name} has no active device to carry them (device turned off, persona offline). Keep track by hand. The host starts launching IC; if it leaves the host, the demigod converges at once (SR5 p. 247).
SR5.MatrixConvergenceSprite: A sprite converged on vanishes, even with tasks left (SR5 p. 254).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeReached: {name} reaches {score} Overwatch Score: the convergence threshold ({threshold}, SR5 p. 232).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeForced: {name} critically glitches while redefining ownership: the grid converges at once (Data Trails p. 154).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeGrid: On the grid: 12 DV of Matrix damage to resist, forced reboot (marks erased, Overwatch Score back to 0) and ejection, with dumpshock in hot-sim or cold-sim VR.
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeHost: In the host {host}: no damage, no ejection; the host puts 3 marks on the persona and starts launching IC. Leaving the host, the convergence happens normally (SR5 p. 247, Kill Code p. 29).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeSecurity: Up to you: the demiGOD gives the physical location to the owner of the grid (and of the host); the security forces in the area converge on it (SR5 p. 232, Kill Code p. 29).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeWanted: Wanted by GOD: a high-threat response team of the grid's authorities is sent after it (Data Trails p. 49).
SR5.ConvergenceNoticeAI: AI: on the grid, what follows depends on its SIN, and a deviceless AI may be hit until it is dissipated (Data Trails p. 152).
SR5.ConvergenceRefused_offline: {name} has no active device left: off the Matrix, no convergence.
SR5.ConvergenceRefused_below: {name}'s Overwatch Score fell back under the threshold (reboot or jack out): convergence not applied.
SR5.ConvergenceRefused_moved: {name} entered or left a host since the card: convergence not applied, to do again from the sheet or the module.
SR5.SocketUse_grappleEscape: break free from the hold of {target}
SR5.ShopConfigBuyersHint: A player only ever sees the characters they own.
SR5.ShopConfigShadowedHint: Both Megapacks are active: this one holds the same items as the other, so it is unticked by default to avoid listing everything twice.
SR5.ShopConfigShelvesHint: Ticked compendiums are sold. Qualities, spells, powers and other non-goods never are. A compendium added later is sold by default.
SR5.ShopCreationActorHint: The gamemaster put this character in creation: creation caps applied, purchases charged.
SR5.ShopCreationModeHint: Gear is added without being charged: character creation, or fixing an item already paid for.
SR5.ShopDealerSpecialization: Dealer: +2 dice for the Bargaining specialization.
SR5.ShopDefaulting: No Negotiation on the contact sheet: defaulting, Charisma - 1 (SR5 p. 53).
SR5.ShopDerivedPool: Contact sheet left empty: pool read off its Connection (Run Faster p. 180).
SR5.ShopEquipModeHint: GM: place any item on any actor, free and without a transaction. Prototypes and every grade are allowed.
SR5.ShopFenceCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: the wrong people are now interested.
SR5.ShopFenceImmediate: Taken on the spot, no questions asked.
SR5.ShopFenceNoBuyer: No buyer found. Try again later, or through a contact.
SR5.ShopFenceTeamworkHint: Rare goods are easier to place: the availability rating is rolled as a teamwork test and its hits join the search pool (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopGradeGone: {name}: this grade is no longer offered here (at creation: used, standard, alphaware). Remove the line and add it again.
SR5.ShopEssenceConfirmText: {name}: this purchase would take Essence down to {essence}. At 0, the character dies (SR5 p. 52). Confirm anyway?
SR5.ShopMarketClosed: The GM closed the market: buy from the vendors. Pick a shop at the top left.
SR5.ShopOnVehicleHint: Its price depends on the vehicle (Rigger 5.0 p. 155): drag it onto the workshop of the vehicle or drone, which prices and buys it.
SR5.ShopOnWeaponHint: Its price depends on the weapon (Hard Targets p. 180-182, SR5 p. 432): drag it onto the weapon's Armory, which prices and buys it.
SR5.ShopOddsHint: A landmark, not a probability: green when the pool beats the Availability by 2 or more, orange within 1, red below (Negotiation + Charisma [Social] vs Availability, SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopOverrideLimitHint: Limit typed in by hand: replaces the computed one. Leave empty to compute it.
SR5.ShopOverridePoolHint: Dice pool typed in by hand: replaces the computed one for the availability test. Leave empty to compute it.
SR5.ShopPartialPool: Charisma missing from the contact sheet: read off its Connection (Run Faster p. 180).
SR5.ShopPurchaseDescription: Bought from the compendium browser: {name}, for {price}¥.
SR5.ShopRetryHint: Failure: the test may be tried again after twice the search time (SR5 p. 418). The GM checks the wait and rolls the test.
SR5.ShopRetryText: Same searcher, same item. You may change the surcharge offered (% of the price); the GM rolls the test.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_unknown: New test refused for {name}: the GM did not record when this failure happened (card missing from their ledger).
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_used: New test refused for {name}: this failure was already tried again.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_early: New test refused for {name}: wait twice the search time, until {date}.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_notFailed: New test refused for {name}: the GM’s ledger records no failure for this line (a critical glitch gives none).
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorGone: New test refused for {name}: the vendor no longer exists.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorClosed: New test refused for {name}: the vendor’s shop is closed.
SR5.ShopRetryRefused_vendorCeiling: New test refused for {name}: its Availability is over the vendor’s ceiling.
SR5.ShopSentToActiveGM: Request passed to the active GM ({name}): their browser keeps the shop's ledger.
SR5.ShopOrderActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM delivers an order: their browser keeps the shop's ledger.
SR5.ShopTestSent: Availability test sent to the GM: they roll the dice and post the card.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorGone: Availability test refused: the vendor no longer exists.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorClosed: Availability test refused: the vendor’s shop is closed.
SR5.ShopTestRefused_vendorCeiling: Availability test refused for {name}: its Availability is over the vendor’s ceiling.
SR5.WARN_ShopTestNoGM: No GM connected: the availability test is rolled by the GM and did not happen. Try again when a GM is here.
SR5.WARN_ShopCardNotByGM: This card was not rolled by the GM: it cannot be cashed. Test the availability again.
SR5.ShopSaleGone: Nothing sold: the goods were no longer there.
SR5.ShopSellOnMarketHint: Extended Etiquette + Charisma [Social] test to find a buyer, then haggling over the price (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopSellToContactHint: The contact takes the goods on the spot, no test, for a share of the listed price per point of Loyalty (SR5 p. 419).
SR5.ShopVendorApproveText: {user} wants to buy for {actor}: {name}, {price}¥. Accept the sale?
SR5.ShopVendorBannerHint: Wide 3:1 image shown at the top of the shop.
SR5.ShopVendorBuyAllHint: Unticked, the vendor only buys what it sells (its shelves).
SR5.ShopVendorChatFree: {actor} receives {name} from {shop}'s stock, free of charge.
SR5.ShopVendorClearConfirm: Delete the {count} item(s) in {name}'s stock? The cashbox is left alone.
SR5.ShopVendorClientsHint: The characters for whom this vendor is a contact, and their Loyalty: only they sell at 5% × Loyalty (SR5 p. 419). Kept here by the GM, never read off the player's sheet.
SR5.ShopVendorRefusesBuyer: This vendor refuses to sell to this buyer.
SR5.ShopVendorContactEmpty: drop a contact on the vendor
SR5.ShopVendorContactHint: The contact who looks for what the vendor does not stock: its Connection gives its pool (Run Faster p. 180). Without one, the vendor's sheet. Dropping a contact on the shop window makes it the searcher.
SR5.ShopVendorLinkedHint: Linked: one stock, however many tokens. Unlinked: each token is a shop of its own.
SR5.ShopVendorMarginHint: Added to the book price (negative for a discounter). The GM adjusts prices to the local market (SR5 p. 417).
SR5.ShopVendorMaxAvailabilityHint: Ceiling of the automatic restock; an item placed by hand may exceed it. 0 = no ceiling.
SR5.ShopVendorNoActor: Put this storage on an NPC (Grunt): it is the one selling.
SR5.ShopVendorNoBanner: No banner of this template in the chosen folder.
SR5.ShopVendorNoBannerFolder: No banner folder: set "Shop: banner folder" in the world settings.
SR5.ShopVendorOfferContact: Contact {name}, Loyalty {loyalty}: {percent}% of the listed price, no test (SR5 p. 419).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: the vendor is insulted, and maybe worse (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferGlitch: Glitch: the vendor is annoyed, the sale may be compromised (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopVendorOfferHaggle: Negotiation: {hits} hits ({pool} dice) against {vendorHits} ({vendorPool} dice): {percent}% of the listed price (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopVendorOnOrderHint: Items of its shelves it does not stock show as "on order": the vendor looks for them with its own Negotiation and Charisma (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_name: price proposed from the name, on the shelves
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_sheet: price proposed from the character's sheet
SR5.ShopVendorOrigin_source: price proposed from the source the item declares
SR5.ShopVendorOverflow: Cashbox full: {amount}¥ went to the vendor's accounts.
SR5.ShopVendorPoolHint: The vendor's Negotiation + Charisma when its sheet is empty (0 = the sheet). Templates give 8: a professional Grunt, a choice of play.
SR5.ShopVendorRestockReading: {name}: reading the shelves for the restock… (up to a minute after a reload)
SR5.ShopVendorRestockBusy: {name}: a restock is already running, wait for it to finish.
SR5.ShopVendorReviewText: {seller} sells for {price}¥. Check each item against its source, then accept, refuse or correct the price.
SR5.ShopVendorSearches: {name} looks for what is not on the shelves (SR5 p. 418).
SR5.ShopVendorSellHint: The GM makes the offer: a contact standing for this vendor takes it at 5% × Loyalty, otherwise an opposed Negotiation test, 25% ± 5% per net hit (SR5 p. 419). The vendor is there: no search for a buyer.
SR5.ShopVendorTemplateHint: The template sets shelves, legality, margin and max availability: choices of play, not rules. Everything stays editable on the storage sheet. The Magic shelf holds foci only, the only magic goods the compendiums sell.
SR5.ShopWindowFailed: The shop could not open: see the console (F12).
SR5.AggravatedWoundBox: Aggravated wound: counts double for healing (right-click to remove the mark)
SR5.WARN_ButtonClaimed: Another owner of this character is already using this button: wait for their card (if nothing comes, try again in a minute).
SR5.WARN_CapBallRoundByRound: Cap & Ball: in combat this weapon reloads round by round (3 Complex Actions per round).
SR5.INFO_CapBallStep: Cap & Ball: reloading {done}/{total}. Stopping before the end means starting over.
SR5.WARN_DroneWirelessOnGMOnly: Only the drone's owner and the gamemaster turn its wireless back on.
SR5.INFO_AmmoAlreadyFull: The weapon is already full: nothing to reload.
SR5.INFO_SourceModifiersCleaned: SR5 migration done: computed modifiers removed from the stored data (actors: {actors}, world items: {items}, unlinked tokens: {tokens}).
SR5.INFO_MigrationStart: Applying SR5 System Migration for version {version}. Please be patient and do not close your game or shut down your server.
SR5.INFO_MigrationDone: SR5 System Migration to version {version} completed!
SR5.INFO_MegapackLiteInSystem: The Megapack SR5 Lite is now part of the system: you can turn the 'Megapack SR5 Lite' module off. The actors and items already drawn from it keep their links and images.
SR5.INFO_SourceModifiersRunning: SR5 migration running: cleaning the computed modifiers stored in the actors. This may take a minute; do not close the world.
SR5.WARN_SourceModifiersDeferred: SR5 migration put off: a combat is under way or has its initiatives rolled. It will run at the next load of the world with no combat and no initiative rolled.
SR5.WARN_SourceModifiersFailed: SR5 migration incomplete: {failed} element(s) could not be cleaned (see the console). It will be taken up again at the next load of the world.
SR5.NativeEffectIgnored: This Foundry effect is ignored by the Shadowrun 5 system: its changes do not apply. For a bonus or a penalty, use an item of type "Effect" (see the wiki, Known limitations).
SR5.NativeEffectIgnoredBanner: The Shadowrun 5 system ignores Foundry's effects: the changes in this window do not apply. For a bonus or a penalty, use an item of type "Effect".
SR5.EffectCardRejected: Effect ignored ({item}, card from {user}): it does not come from the caster's owner, or its dice cannot be read. Apply it by hand if needed.
SR5.UnresistedDamageConfirm: {item} deals {value} box(es) to the {monitor} monitor of {actor}, with no resistance test. Apply?
SR5.WARN_UnresistedDamageNotOwner: You do not own this actor: the GM must apply this damage.
SR5.EffectCardConfirm: {user}: {caster}, {item}. Hits counted again on the dice: {hits}, net hits: {netHits}. Apply the effect with these values?
SR5.ToxinCardConfirm: {user}: {toxin} ({weapon}) on {actor}. Power read again: {power}, hits counted again on the dice: {hits}. Damage: {damage}. Effects: {effects}. Apply?

SR5.PushNoEdgeSpent: The card of {actor} says it pushed the limit, but its sheet shows no Edge spent: {hits} hits kept, without Edge nor the Rule of Six (SR5 p. 56).
SR5.MatrixCardNoDamage: The hits counted again on the dice leave no damage to deal.

SR5.INFO_MatrixDamageRelayed: {name} ({item}): {value} matrix damage asked of the GM, who reads the card again before writing it.

SR5.AttackCardRefused: Attack card from {user} refused: its author does not own the attacker, or the weapon, spell or preparation is not on its sheet. Nothing is rolled.
SR5.ResistanceCardRefused: Card refused: only the GM, or an owner of the actor it was rolled for, may resist its damage, and for that actor only.
SR5.AttackCardReread: Attack card from {user} ({actor}, {item}) read again on the sheet; the values read again count.
SR5.AttackCardDV: DV read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed} (SR5 p. 169-171).

SR5.AttackCardAP: AP read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed}.

SR5.AttackCardElement: Element read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed}.
SR5.AttackCardSource: Source read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed}.
SR5.AttackCardHits: Hits counted again on the dice: {value}, the card claimed {claimed} (pool worked out on the sheet, Edge included).
SR5.AttackCardForce: Force read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed} (at most Magic × 2 and what the card's Drain allows, SR5 p. 278-282).
SR5.AttackCardFallOff: Blast read again: {value} per meter, the card claimed {claimed} (SR5 p. 182).
SR5.AttackCardToxinPower: Toxin Power read again: {value}, the card claimed {claimed}.
SR5.AttackCardCalledShot: Effects of the called shot "{value}" read again on what it allows (DV limit, effects, initiative): the card claimed others.
SR5.AttackCardOvercast: Force {force} above Magic ({magic}): the Drain is Physical (SR5 p. 278).
SR5.AttackCardOverPool: The card shows {dice} dice, the pool worked out on the sheet (Edge included, without situational bonuses) allows {cap}: only the first {cap} count.

SR5.ToxinCardSpent: Toxin effect already applied ({user}'s card, on {actor}).
SR5.EffectDefinitionTitle: Effect defined on a player’s sheet
SR5.EffectDefinitionIntro: {item}, on {owner}’s sheet, is about to apply to {actor}:
SR5.EffectDefinitionIntroArea: {item}, on {owner}’s sheet, is about to apply to the tokens of its template (the first: {actor}). Your answer stands for the whole template:
SR5.EffectDefinitionNoResistance: No resistance test: the sheet says this spell is not resisted.
SR5.EffectDefinitionNoReference: No reference found (compendium or world item): check the sheet before applying.
SR5.EffectDefinitionRefResisted: The reference calls for a resistance test: cancel to have the target resist.
SR5.EffectDefinitionRefNotResisted: The sheet calls for a resistance test, the reference does not.

SR5.EffectCardOverPool: The card shows more dice than the pool worked out again ({allowed}, Edge included): only the first ones count.
SR5.EffectCardItemMismatch: {item}: the caster's sheet holds {written} hits, the dice of his card give {hits}. The template applies {hits}.
SR5.TemplateFlagsIgnored: Template from {user} ({item}): the light, visibility, noise or background count written on it are ignored. Only the ones its item gives count. Place a template yourself if the scene calls for it.
SR5.ThresholdModifierHint: added to the threshold of the test if it has one, no effect on a test without threshold.
SR5.AimForPerfectionReminder: Aim for Perfection: pick a Called Shot, unless laying down cover fire or doing something a Called Shot does not fit (Assassin's Primer (French edition) p. 15).
SR5.WARN_VintageElectronic: {weapon} is a Vintage weapon: {accessory} will have no wireless effect on it (Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3).
SR5.WARN_BundleWirelessOn: "{name}" is part of an augmentation bundle: its wireless cannot be turned off (Chrome Flesh p. 92).
SR5.WoundResolveEffect: Deus vult! / My Country: Willpower test against wound modifiers
SR5.DelicateFingersEffect: Delicate Fingers: no penalty for gear not sized for a troll
SR5.WoundResolveAsk: {name} was wounded since their last action phase, or is already holding: Willpower test, threshold {threshold}. On a success they ignore all wound modifiers; on a failure they apply at once and the advantage is lost until the next combat (Assassin's Primer (French edition) p. 14-15).
SR5.WoundResolveBroken: Test failed: the wound modifiers of {name} apply until the end of the combat.
SR5.WARN_VintageNoWireless: A Vintage weapon can never go wireless (Gun H(e)aven 3 p. 3).
SR5.INFO_EngulfSourceMissing: Engulf: the spirit's attack cannot be found, the DV cannot be worked out again. Resist it by hand (spirit's Magic × 2, SR5 p. 396).
SR5.RADIATION_SceneHint: Radiation severity of the scene (Run & Gun p. 152). Nothing happens without the button: it opens the list of exposed characters.
SR5.RADIATION_Exposed: {actor}: exposed, feels a {level} severity; first test on {time}.
SR5.RADIATION_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the radiation ledger.
SR5.RADIATION_OutcomeStunOne: {actor}: Power {power}, {hits} hits, 1 Stun box and Nausea.
SR5.RADIATION_OutcomeStun: {actor}: Power {power}, {hits} hits, {remaining} Stun boxes and Nausea.
SR5.RADIATION_Reminders: Reminders (Run & Gun p. 152), not automated: after a Severe or worse exposure the character radiates within 10 m himself. No healing test in a radioactive zone. Moderate: unconscious after 72 h, dead 72 h later.
SR5.AntitoxinNeutralized: Neutralized by the antitoxin: no effect
SR5.Anticoagulant_GE:
The critter’s attack carries some form of anti-coagulant that keeps the target’s blood from clotting. Once hit with this power, the victim’s blood continues to flow, causing two boxes of Stun damage every minute that cannot be resisted. The bleeding can be stopped with a medkit (or better medical equipment) and a First Aid + Logic [Mental] (3) Test.

Critter power: wounds stop clotting. The victim takes 2 boxes of Stun damage per minute, unresisted, until a First Aid + Logic [Mental] (3) Test with a medkit or better.

Howling Shadows p. 193
SR5.AssensingResult1a: The general state of the subject’s health (healthy, injured, ill, etc.).
SR5.AssensingResult1b: The subject’s general emotional state or impression (happy, sad, angry, etc.).
SR5.AssensingResult1c: Whether the subject is mundane or Awakened.
SR5.AssensingResult2a: The presence and location of cyberware implants.
SR5.AssensingResult2b: The class of a magical subject (fire elemental, manipulation spell, power focus, curse ritual, and so on).
SR5.AssensingResult2c: If you have seen the subject’s aura before, you may recognize it, regardless of physical disguises or alterations
SR5.AssensingResult3a: The presence and location of alphaware cyber implants.
SR5.AssensingResult3b: Whether the subject’s Essence, Magic and Force are higher, lower, or equal to your own.
SR5.AssensingResult3c: A general diagnosis for any maladies (diseases or toxins) the subject suffers.
SR5.AssensingResult3d: Any astral signatures present on the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult4a: The presence and location of bioware implants and betaware cyber implants.
SR5.AssensingResult4b: The exact Essence, Magic, and Force of the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult4c: The general cause of any astral signature (combat spell, alchemical combat spell, air spirit, and so on).
SR5.AssensingResult5a: The presence and location of deltaware implants, gene treatments, and nanotech.
SR5.AssensingResult5b: An accurate diagnosis of any disease or toxins which afflict the subject.
SR5.AssensingResult5c: The fact that a subject is a technomancer.
SR5.AstralProjectionLimit_D: (Magic × 2) hours (SR5 p. 314); + initiate grade with Improved Astral Form; in days with Astralnaut (Forbidden Arcana p. 44).
SR5.AttackModFiringFromVehicle: Attacker firing from a moving vehicle
SR5.AttackModFiringWithImagingDevice: Attacker firing from cover with imaging device
SR5.VisionEnhancements_D: Vision enhancements mounted in the accessory, each taking its Capacity (Core Rulebook p. 431 and 444). A Capacity of 0 takes the book's: imaging scope and periscope 3, smartgun 1.
SR5.WARN_AccessoryCapacityFull: Not enough Capacity left in this accessory for this enhancement (Core Rulebook p. 444).
SR5.ManualMissing: The manual compendiums (sr5.manual, sr5.manuel) are not installed.
SR5.ManualEmpty: The manual is empty in this copy of the system, which was not compiled. The GM closes Foundry, runs "npm run build:packs" in the system folder, then restarts Foundry; or install the published system from its manifest. The manual also comes as a PDF attached to the release.
SR5.CompendiumDrawBrowserHint: Draws at random among everything the filters let through, every page included.
SR5.CompendiumDrawEmpty: Nothing to draw: no entry matches.
SR5.CompendiumDrawPrompt: Draw at random among the {count} entries of "{name}", each as likely as the others.
SR5.CompendiumBrowserFailed: The compendium browser could not be opened. See the console for details.
SR5.ChooseItemToPan: Choose item to add to PAN
SR5.ClickForDetails: Click here to display or hide details
SR5.GrappleReversed: Situation reversed: {holder} now holds {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold} (Run & Gun p. 112).
SR5.GrappleClinchTaken: {holder} clinches {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}. {holder} has the superior position; Reach cancelled between them; melee weapons: penalty equal to their Reach, firearms: penalty of {hold}; they only move together, 2 m per action (Run & Gun p. 120).
SR5.HELP_GrappleClinchMsg: Clinch: Agility + Gymnastics [Physical] against Reaction + Intuition (Run & Gun p. 119). Target the opponent. Requires martial arts training.
SR5.GrappleHoldChanged: {holder}'s hold on {held} is now {hold}. To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}.
SR5.GrappleHoldTaken: {holder} subdues {held} (hold: {hold}). To break free: Escape, threshold {hold}. Keeping the hold costs a Complex Action each action phase (SR5 p. 195).
SR5.GrappleNoHold: No hold: Strength and net hits do not exceed the Physical limit
SR5.SETTINGS_GrapplingRules_D: Clinch, subdue, escape and reversal (SR5 p. 195, Run & Gun p. 112 and 119-124): linked statuses on the tokens and computed thresholds. Unchecked, nothing changes.
SR5.SETTINGS_RunningFromDistance_D: Running (SR5 p. 161-162): the "Running" status is put on when a token in combat is moved with the "Run" or "Sprint" action. Checked, it is also put on as soon as the token has gone farther than its walking rate this Combat Turn. Unchecked by default: a token moved by hand to tidy the map would count as running.
SR5.SETTINGS_RunningFromDistance_T: Put the "Running" status on from the distance covered
SR5.WARN_GrappleAlreadyHeld: One of the fighters is already in a hold: one hold per token.
SR5.WARN_GrappleHoldChanged: The hold has changed since this roll: this button no longer applies.
SR5.WARN_GrappleNotYourHold: Only the GM and the owner of the one holding can use these buttons.
SR5.WARN_GrappleNeedsMartialArts: The clinch requires martial arts training (Run & Gun p. 119): this character has none. The GM decides.
SR5.CyberEyesReplacedVision: Cybereyes: the vision of the metatype is replaced.
SR5.CyberlimbNoticeIntro: Cyberlimbs (SR5 p. 456-457): a Strength or Agility enhancement plugged into a cyberlimb now raises that limb only, no longer the whole body. These characters carry one:
SR5.CyberlimbNoticeHowTo: For a weapon to use the limb, open its sheet and choose the limb in "Held by" (configuration tab). This message shows only once in this world.
SR5.LivingPersonaManaged: Kept by the system: rating = Resonance, attributes from the mental attributes (SR5 p. 251).
SR5.MatrixFusionSlave: One with the Matrix: slaved persona (KC p. 97)
SR5.MatrixFusionMaster: One with the Matrix: persona masters a PAN (KC p. 97)
SR5.HELP_MatrixFusionMsg:
A living persona is no device: without this quality it has no PAN (SR5 p. 251).

Kill Code p. 97: at 2 karma it may be slaved to a deck's or commlink's PAN; at 8 karma it may master a PAN of Resonance × 3 devices; at 10 karma, both.

The system first reads the quality on the sheet (system effect "One with the Matrix"); this choice only counts when it is not there.
SR5.EchoResonantDissonance: Echo: Resonant Dissonance (Better Than Bad p. 161)
SR5.HELP_VehicleCurrentSpeedMsg: The Speed the vehicle is moving at right now, 0 when it stands still. Read by Speed Demon (Speed 3 or more, 4 for aircraft) and Information Overload (four vehicles moving).
SR5.HELP_MachinistSharing: Machinist (Kill Code p. 90): the living persona acts as a rigger command console, its Sharing equals Charisma.
SR5.HELP_MachinistNoiseReduction: Machinist (Kill Code p. 90): the living persona acts as a rigger command console, its Noise Reduction equals Willpower.
SR5.CalledShotSkillsHint: Attacks whose called shot penalty the technique lowers
SR5.AIProgramsNoDevice: No programs outside a device (Data Trails p. 152)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_NoDevice: The AI was on no device: it resists with Willpower + Depth (Data Trails p. 155).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_OnDevice: The AI ran on a device that is not bricked: it resists with Willpower + Firewall + Depth (Data Trails p. 155).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Bricked: The device {device} is bricked: no Firewall, and its Device Rating ({rating}) is added to the Essence to resist (Data Trails p. 156).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_EdgeEscape: Before resolving: the AI may burn 1 point of Edge to jump to a grid and escape the dissipation; it then loses a random advanced program. If so, do not resolve this card.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Rule: The AI always loses 1 point of Essence, plus 1 per box of overflow damage not resisted. It also loses 1 point of Depth (minimum 1).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Surplus: Overflow damage (boxes beyond the monitor, to check)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_SurplusFromPlayer: This overflow was worked out by a player's client: check it.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_DeviceRatingAdded: + {rating} (rating of the bricked device) to resist
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Extra: Extra dice, or fewer (HELLO WORLD!: +1 per rank, Data Trails p. 147)
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Result: {pool} dice, {hits} hits against {toResist} to resist: {loss} point(s) of Essence lost.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Reminders: Left to the GM: remove a random advanced program (never learned again) and give a Fragmentation trait if Essence was lost, once per event (Data Trails p. 155).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Destroyed: Essence at 0: the core is too corrupted to be restored, the AI is destroyed (Data Trails p. 155).
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_Gone: This AI no longer exists, or is no longer an AI.
SR5.AIDISSIPATION_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM can resolve a dissipation.

SR5.WARN_ShopOrderRejectedKept: {name}: order kept on {actor}'s sheet, already paid. Cancel it to refund.
SR5.ImplantRejectedConfirmText: {actor}'s body rejects bioware ({quality}, SR5 p. 83): {names}. Install anyway?

SR5.WARN_BoneClashSwitchedOff: {user} switched {name} on in {actor}'s sheet, beside {lacing}: one type of bone lacing only, and never with bone density augmentation (SR5 p. 455 and 459). Switched off again.

SR5.WARN_ShopAccessoryOnWeapon: {name} is bought on a weapon's Armory, at its price on that weapon.

SR5.HELP_IceHostMsg: The host this IC runs in (SR5 p. 246-247: IC are programs of the host). Chosen by the gamemaster. The PAN crown of the IC draws the line up to its host, and modules read it in system.matrix.hostUuid.
SR5.HELP_PanMasterMsg: The host or the master device (commlink, cyberdeck, rigger command console) this device is slaved to (SR5 p. 233). A host slaves as many devices as it likes, at any distance; a commlink or a cyberdeck, its rating × 3 at most. The PAN crown draws the line from the device to its master.
SR5.EffectFlickerDisconnectedTarget: Avatar left in the Matrix, unable to act, for {turns} combat turn(s) (Kill Code p. 67)
SR5.INFO_FlickerDisconnected: {name} is disconnected from the Matrix by the Flicker: the avatar stays, inert, for {turns} combat turn(s) or until the device reboots.
SR5.WARN_FlickerDisconnected: Disconnected by a Flicker: the avatar cannot act until it vanishes or the device reboots (Kill Code p. 67).
SR5.HELP_ShowAllMastersMsg: Unchecked, the list offers only the actors with a token on this device's scene, unlinked tokens included, each under its token's name. Checked, it offers every actor of the world.
SR5.HELP_HostSlavesMsg: The devices slaved to this host (SR5 p. 233: a host has no limit). "Slave the scene's devices" takes at once every device of its scene with no master; "Slave the selection" takes the selected tokens; "Slave…" lets you choose. You may also drop a token or an actor here. "Release" frees a device.
SR5.INFO_HostNoFreeSlave: No device without a master on {host}'s scene.
SR5.INFO_HostSlaveRefused: {name} cannot be slaved to this host.
SR5.HostEnterNoMark: Entering {host} takes a mark on it (SR5 p. 239).
SR5.HostLeft: Leaves the host {host}, back to the grid.
SR5.HostLeftAfterConvergence: {name} leaves the host after the convergence: the grid's demiGOD converges on them at once (SR5 p. 247).
SR5.DeckUnconfigured: Deck not configured: drag the attribute array values onto Attack, Sleaze, Data Processing and Firewall (SR5 p. 228). An unassigned attribute is 0, and so is the limit that uses it.
SR5.DIALOG_WarningNoAmmoType:
{actor} does not have {ammoType} for {weaponType} in his inventory.
Do you still want to reload {itemName}?
SR5.DIALOG_WarningPermanentDelete:
You are about to delete a '{type}' item from the inventory of the '{actor}' actor. This action cannot be undone.

Are you sure you wish to delete '{itemName}'?
SR5.TraditionHybridHint: Hybrid tradition (Forbidden Arcana p. 101): the drain attribute and the spirits stay those of the tradition that gives the paradigm; only the ideals, the mentor spirit and the favored spells may come from the other tradition (the rest, with the GM's approval). To make one: copy the paradigm's tradition and rename it.
SR5.DrugCrashPhysical: The crashes will deal Physical damage rather than Stun
SR5.DrugOverdoseInfo: {actor}: overdose ({drugs}), {value}S to resist with Body + Willpower (SR5 p. 415).
SR5.CyberpsychosisGlitch: Cyberpsychosis: the character acts inappropriately or overreacts violently (Chrome Flesh p. 57)
SR5.CyberpsychosisCriticalGlitch: Cyberpsychosis: psychotic break, the gamemaster decides what the character does until recovery (Chrome Flesh p. 57)
SR5.WARN_DrugDesignRefused: The GM refused {drug}: it cannot be taken.
SR5.DrugDesignerIntro: Custom drugs (Chrome Flesh p. 190-191): pick a base, then blocks and their level, then enhancers. The drug is worked out as you go.
SR5.DrugDesignerDescription: Custom drug, made with the drug designer by the rules of Chrome Flesh (p. 190-191).
SR5.DrugDesignerAttributeFloor: An attribute does not go below 1: a drug that would bring it to 0 or less paralyses the character while it lasts (Chrome Flesh p. 190).
SR5.DrugDesignerHasErrors: The recipe breaks a rule of Chrome Flesh: fix it before going on.
SR5.DrugDesignerPendingHint: Drug submitted by a player: check the recipe (you may adjust it), then approve or refuse it.
SR5.DrugDesignerRequest: {user} submits a drug designed for {actor}: {drug}. It cannot be taken before you approve it.
SR5.INFO_DrugDesignerSubmitted: Drug {drug} submitted to the GM: it awaits approval.
SR5.WARN_DrugDesignerNoSkill: Only the GM, or the owner of a character with the Chemistry skill, can design a drug.
SR5.WARN_DrugDesignNotApproved: {drug} awaits the GM's approval: it cannot be taken yet.
SR5.WARN_DrugDesignGMOnly: Only the GM approves or refuses a designed drug.
SR5.DrugDesignerError_incompatible: Block {block} lowers {attribute}, which block {other} raises: they are incompatible (Chrome Flesh p. 190).
SR5.DrugDesignerError_loweredByBase: The base lowers {attribute}: block {block}, which raises it, goes no higher than level {max} (Chrome Flesh p. 191).
SR5.DrugDesignerError_initiative: No more than +{max}D6 Initiative (Chrome Flesh p. 191).
SR5.DrugDesignerError_attributeBonus: {attribute}: no more than +{max}, all sources together (Chrome Flesh p. 191).
SR5.DrugDesignerError_enhancer: An enhancer is taken {max} times at most (Chrome Flesh p. 191).
SR5.DrugPreparedForHint: Designer (Chrome Flesh p. 190): anyone else takes it as a street-cooked drug
SR5.WARN_DrugWithoutStat: {actor} takes {drug}, which has no drug stat: neither its duration nor its crash will be counted, and the calendar will not warn. Give it a system effect of the "Drug" category, or follow it by hand.
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_CardBackground: Background count {rating} over {radius} m (temporary: -1 per hour; permanent if anyone died).
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_CardTarget: Against the object it is placed on: {dv}P (×{multiplier}), Armor halved.
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_Detonate: Place the blast and set it off
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_DetonatorFailed: The detonator failed: the charge does not go off and stays in place.
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_Dud: Rating 0: the charge does not explode.
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_Estimate: Homemade explosive: estimate on the announced rating, the GM works out the real explosion.
SR5.EXPLOSIVE_GasLeak: Gas leak or fuel set alight (+20P)

SR5.ElementalDamageElectricity_GE:
An electrical attack that deals damage stuns the target: -1 die to all its actions and defense tests (not to damage resistance tests) for one combat turn, and an immediate -5 to its Initiative score.

These effects do not stack: each further electrical attack that deals damage while they last extends the penalty by one combat turn. An Initiative brought to 0 or less loses the last action; if it already was, the reduction applies at the start of the next combat turn (SR5 p. 170).

If the electrical attack deals at least one box, the target immediately loses 5 Initiative and takes -1 die on actions and defense tests (not damage resistance) for 1 Combat Turn. The effects do not add up: each further electrical hit during that time extends the penalty by one turn. Initiative at 0 or less: the last action is lost; if it was already there, the -5 hits the next Combat Turn.

SR5 p. 170

SR5.IceAcid_GE:
Acid IC targets and overwrites your protective software. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Firewall by 1. If your Firewall has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.

Each attack with at least 1 net hit lowers the target's Firewall by 1. Once Firewall is at 0, it deals 1 DV of Matrix damage per net hit instead. Losses stack until the device reboots.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceBinder_GE:
Binder IC corrupts your base operating system. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Data Processing by 1. If your Data Processing has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.

Each attack with at least 1 net hit lowers the target's Data Processing by 1. Once that attribute is at 0, it deals 1 DV of Matrix damage per net hit instead. Losses stack until the device reboots.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceBlack_GE:
Black IC is the most feared intrusion countermeasures program on the market. The hosts that run it don’t want you repelled—they want you dead. When it hits, Black IC link-locks you. It also causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target) along with an equal amount of biofeedback damage.

A successful attack link-locks the target and deals DV = Attack + 1 per net hit + 2 per host mark on it as Matrix damage, plus the same amount of physical biofeedback.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceBlaster_GE:
Also known as Grey IC, a Blaster IC program’s attack causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage, +1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target, with biofeedback damage. The biofeedback from a Blaster program can only cause Stun damage. A single successful attack also link-locks the target.

Also called grey IC. A successful attack link-locks the target and deals DV = Attack + 1 per net hit + 2 per mark as Matrix damage, plus the same amount of biofeedback, always Stun.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceBloodhound_GE:
A mix of Patrol and Track IC: it watches the host and, as soon as it spots illegal activity, tries to put two or more marks on the culprit to learn their physical location. While it is tracking, it no longer patrols.

DT p. 76
SR5.IceBlueGoo_GE:
If an avatar successfully deals Matrix damage to this IC, it deactivates by exploding. Make a Host Rating x 2 [Attack] v. Logic + Firewall Opposed Test. If this attack hits, the avatar is link-locked by the host that launched the Blue Goo. The avatar must resist (Attack) DV, and it is marked by the host. The avatar must successfully Jack Out of the host to end the link-lock.

When an avatar deals Matrix damage to it, it blows up and is gone: the host rolls Rating × 2 [Attack] against Logic + Firewall. On a hit, the avatar resists DV = Attack, gets a host mark and stays link-locked until it manages to jack out.

KC p. 68
SR5.IceCatapult_GE:
With net hits, it lowers the target's Firewall by 1 (restored on reboot) and deals as many boxes of Stun as net hits, +1 per mark. It does not link-lock.

DT p. 76
SR5.IceCrash_GE:
If Crash IC has a mark on you (through its host) and hits, one of your programs crashes, selected at random. Programs crashed this way can’t be run again until after a reboot.

If the host has a mark on the target and the attack gets at least 1 net hit, one of the target's running programs, chosen at random, crashes; it cannot run again until a reboot.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceFlicker_GE:
Flicker link-locks you when it hits and puts a mark on you. If you have two marks on you, it disconnects you from the Matrix, dealing dumpshock damage if appropriate. Although you have been disconnected from the Matrix, your avatar doesn’t disappear until you log back in using the same device, or after [Device Rating] rounds. It remains where you left it, unable to act, while other IC can attempt to trace your location or analyze your avatar.

A successful attack link-locks and places a mark. At two marks, the target is dropped from the Matrix (dumpshock if relevant), but their avatar stays behind, inert, for [Device Rating] rounds or until they log back in with the same device: other IC can still analyze or trace it.

KC p. 67
SR5.IceJammer_GE:
Jammer IC turns your firewall against your own attacks. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Attack by 1. If your Attack has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.

Each attack with at least 1 net hit lowers the target's Attack by 1. Once Attack is at 0, it deals 1 DV of Matrix damage per net hit instead. Losses stack until the device reboots.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceKiller_GE:
This IC is a simple but effective cybercombat program that causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark) on the target with each successful attack.

Basic cybercombat IC: each successful attack deals DV = Attack + 1 per net hit + 2 per mark as Matrix damage.

SR5.IceMarker_GE:
Marker IC installs tiny worm programs that mess with your datastreams. When it gets 1 or more net hits on its attack, it reduces your Sleaze by 1. If your Sleaze has been reduced to 0 already, it causes 1 DV Matrix damage per net hit on the attack. The reduction is cumulative and lasts until you reboot the targeted device.

Each attack with at least 1 net hit lowers the target's Sleaze by 1. Once Sleaze is at 0, it deals 1 DV of Matrix damage per net hit instead. Losses stack until the device reboots.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IcePatrol_GE:
Patrol IC acts more like an agent than other intrusion countermeasures. Its job is to patrol a host, scanning people’s marks and looking for illegal activity using the Matrix Perception action on all targets in the host. While the act of placing a mark is an illegal activity, the act of simply having a mark is not. Once you have the mark, you are considered a legitimate user. Patrol IC has no attack, but it shares its information with its parent host. Since the Patrol IC doesn’t use Attack actions, it doesn’t take Matrix damage when it fails. Most hosts have Patrol IC and keep it running all the time.

Never attacks: it runs Matrix Perception on the icons in the host to find intruders and passes what it sees to the host. A mark already in place counts as legitimate access; placing one is what is illegal. It takes no damage when it fails. Almost every host keeps one running at all times.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceProbe_GE:
The task of Probe IC is to mark intruders for other IC. Every successful “attack” means another mark for the host and its IC on the target, up to the maximum of three marks.

Each successful "attack" gives the host and its IC one more mark on the target, up to three.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceScramble_GE:
Scramble IC nukes your connection to the Matrix and forces you to reboot. If the host has three marks on you when this IC hits you, you reboot immediately, taking dumpshock if you were in VR.

If the host has three marks on the target and the attack gets at least 1 net hit, the target's device reboots at once; in VR, dumpshock follows.

SR5 p. 248
SR5.IceShocker_GE:
Deals no Matrix damage: a successful attack takes 5 off the target's Initiative Score. Often run alongside other IC.

DT p. 76
SR5.IceSleuther_GE:
This IC puts a mark on you if it hits. Each mark provides a legitimate user with +2 dice on any Matrix Search actions or Matrix Perception tests involving you. It works by applying different behavioral algorithms and heuristics to try to work out what sort of person you are. This IC also installs tracker code into your avatar, enabling the IC to identify which grids and hosts your avatar visits after the mark lands. Marks from this IC may be removed normally

A successful attack places a mark; each mark gives the legitimate user +2 dice on Matrix Search and Matrix Perception aimed at the target. While the mark stays, the IC knows which grids and hosts the avatar visits. These marks can be erased normally.

SR5.IceSparky_GE:
Sparky IC is also known as “Psycho Killer,” an upgraded version of the popular Killer IC. It causes (Attack) DV Matrix damage (+1 DV per net hit and +2 DV per mark on the target) with biofeedback damage.

A stronger Killer: each successful attack deals DV = Attack + 1 per net hit + 2 per mark as Matrix damage, plus the same amount of biofeedback.

SR5.IceTarBaby_GE:
The Tar Baby IC link-locks you when it hits. If you’re already link-locked, it puts a mark on you, up to a maximum of three marks.

A successful attack link-locks the target; if it already is, the IC places a mark instead, up to three.

SR5.IceTrack_GE:
Track IC follows the datastreams between your icon and your deck. If this IC hits and the host has two marks or more on you, the host (and its owners) discover your physical location, which is usually reported to real-world authorities immediately.

If the attack gets at least 1 net hit and the host has two or more marks on the persona, the host and its owners learn where the character physically is, and usually report it to the authorities.

SR5.LifestyleComforts_GE:
Comforts & Necessities are an integral part of any lifestyle. If a shadowrunner doesn’t get a good night’s rest and a belly full of nutrient-added soy, he’ll eventually end up at the morgue. This is because of the possibility of fatigue damage (p. 172, SR5). At the beginning of most game sessions, characters roll to resist fatigue damage, simulating how much rest they have been able to get in their quarters. Characters do not, however, have to make this roll if the new session directly continues an adventure from the previous one and they have not had a chance to rest in whatever domicile is part of their lifestyle. Base Fatigue damage that characters must resist is 6S. For each level in the Comforts & Necessities category, reduce the DV by 2.

Additional factors may affect the damage the character must resist. For example, having allergies can be a hassle, especially food allergies where choices are limited. Allergies to things found in the environment (such as pollution, ultraviolet rays, plastic, etc.) increase the Fatigue damage characters must resist by 1 per level above mild for common allergies and 1 per level above moderate for uncommon allergies if the Comforts & Necessities category of the lifestyle is level three or lower. Allergies to foods can be problematic, as some special dietary requirements may not be available in all lifestyles. Allergies to common foodstuffs (soy, mycoprotein, etc.) also increase the fatigue damage value by 1 per level above mild if the Comforts & Necessities category of the lifestyle is level 3 or lower. For uncommon allergies, the damage value increases by 1 if the allergy is Severe, 2 if it is Extreme.

Start-of-session fatigue: when the character got to rest at home since the last session, they resist 6S fatigue, minus 2 per level of Comforts & Necessities (fatigue: SR5 p. 172). With Comforts & Necessities at 3 or less, an environmental allergy adds +1 DV per degree above Mild (Common) or Moderate (Uncommon), and a common food allergy +1 DV per degree above Mild (Uncommon: +1 if Severe, +2 if Extreme).

Run Faster p. 224
SR5.LifestylePrimary: Main lifestyle: the one the starting nuyen use (SR5 p. 95)
SR5.LifestyleSecurity_GE:
Security covers a broad sense of how much a deterrent your place is to unwanted guests and criminal activities other than your own. Those living on the street can only protect what they can hold on to, while people higher up the lifestyle food chain have a physical location that can store and protect their stuff, rather than having to carry it all around with them all the time. Each point into security reduces the risk of theft of the character’s stuff at home. The exact details of when this comes into play are left up to the gamemaster, but one example is a Security Test representing how well the place is watched by security officers, alarms, and other security measures. If anyone attempts a burglary at the character’s domicile while the character is away, roll a dice pool of (Security level x 2) against the Sneaking + Agility of the burglars. If the Security wins the test, security officers have noticed the attempt, or a home alarm has been triggered, or some other event has occurred to indicate that the burglars ran afoul of the security measures without the player having to do a thing. For reference to various aspects of security besides being armed and dangerous, see p. 355, SR5.

The gamemaster should also look at the rare items the character owns compared to the security of the lifestyle. If the item’s Availability is more than twice the Security level, chances are someone/thing will notice the item and want to steal it. The greater the discrepancy, the more likely the item will be targeted.

The gamemaster is encouraged to decide and roleplay out such events, especially if it helps with the adventure/campaign. Alternatively, the gamemaster can abstract the potential for attempted theft with a test using a dice pool equal to the difference between the minimum Security level of a lifestyle required and the actual Security level purchased by the player. For each hit, the player must pay one percent of the monthly cost of the lifestyle to replace stolen goods or repair damaged properly (or pay insurance premiums that help them deal with such things). Nothing exceedingly valuable should go missing in this test. Burglary of a truly valuable item requires the Security Test detailed above.

Burglary while the character is away: the burglars roll Agility + Sneaking opposed by Security × 2 dice; if Security wins, they are spotted or scared off. Any item whose Availability equals or exceeds the Security level may draw unwanted attention. Quick variant: pool = purchased Security minus the lifestyle's minimum Security; each hit costs 1% of the monthly rent in losses (security: SR5 p. 355).

SR5.LifeStyleZone_A:
Response Time: 2D6 + 3 minutes.

This features high-class residences and corporate buildings.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_AA:
Response Time: 1D6 + 4 minutes.

Here you’ll find luxury-class residences and posh commercial places. If you ask the price, you can’t afford to live here.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_AAA:
Response Time: 1D6 minutes.

Corporate headquarters. Skyraker condos. And the occasional private islands. This is where the world’s wealthiest pay to make sure they’re kept safe.
SR5.LifeStyleZone_B:
Response Time: 1D6 x 5 minutes.

SR5.LifeStyleZone_C:
Response Time: 1D6 x 10 minutes.

The district has seen better days and could use more than just a paint job to bring it up to snuff. You can find low-rent residences, storage facilities, small bodegas, and other similar sites in these zones
SR5.LifeStyleZone_D:
Response Time: 1D6 x 12 minutes.

You can find these zones in the area between industrial and residential districts where the exposure to pollution is a little better than those who live right next to the smoke-churning factories. Or at least, that’s what the residents will tell you. Patrols come through this area, only because it’s inconvenient to go around. SR5.LifeStyleZone_E:
Response Time: 1D6 hours.

SR5.LifeStyleZone_Z:
Response Time: 2D6 hours.

This is a lawless area deep in the heart of many barrens. Criminal organizations and gangs can sometimes feel uneasy here. Awakened critters and toxic spirits tend to roam wild. Unless it’s a big incident, most security providers will find routes to avoid going through Z zones. Any type of residence can be found, though it will be in serious disrepair.
