SR5.MANEUVER_coordinatedEffort_D: A seasoned team plans its actions: +2 dice to ranged attacks, and +2 to a crew's piloting tests.
SR5.MANEUVER_crossfire_D: Two elements take the same target from two angles: +3 attack dice. Choosing the spots is first a plain Small Unit Tactics + Intuition test (simple action).
SR5.MANEUVER_diamond_D: Four members in a diamond, 360° view: +1 die to surprise tests (the GM's) and +2 Initiative.
SR5.MANEUVER_dynamicEntry_D: The team storms a closed space in pairs: +3 attack dice, only +1 if spotted first.
SR5.MANEUVER_explosiveEntry_D: As the dynamic entry, after a grenade thrown into the room: +3 attack dice, +1 if the team was spotted, plus the grenade's effects.
SR5.MANEUVER_fireShield_D: Supporting fire walks ahead of the team: +4 dice for friendly forces under it, -2 dice to the enemy (the GM's). Glitch: scatter; critical glitch: the fire lands on the team. Threshold set by the GM.
SR5.MANEUVER_floatingRearguard_D: A pair stays back and watches; the test's leader is the one behind. +1 die to Perception and +2 Initiative for the watching pair.
SR5.MANEUVER_indirectFire_D: A spotter designates the target to a heavy weapon (Perception + Intuition through an RP-Tac, else Navigation + Intuition): the blind fire penalty becomes -2 (the GM's).
SR5.MANEUVER_packAttack_D: The pack swarms a target: +1 die to melee attacks per 3 hits of the leader.
SR5.MANEUVER_penetratingFire_D: Coordinated attacks on a weak spot, as precise shots: the best attack gains half the AP of the others (the GM's).
SR5.MANEUVER_saturation_D: The team advances firing, then charges: +4 dice to semi-auto, burst or full-auto attacks.
SR5.MANEUVER_shieldWall_D: Shield bearers cover the team: the covered ones add the shield's Armor (the GM's) and get a defense die per net hit. Failure: the formation breaks, no penalty.
SR5.MANEUVER_slicingPie_D: The scout alone works round a corner: +1 defense die per hit, kept while he stays still and the target stays put. Glitch: spotted; critical glitch: spotted and -2 defense dice.
SR5.MANEUVER_targetDesignation_D: A spotter guides an air strike: +2 dice to the aircraft's Gunnery on the target, no environment modifiers (the GM's).
SR5.MatrixActionBreakFile_GE:
Key with no matching action in the books: to remove a file's protection, see Crack File.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionBreakTargetLock_GE:
Passive targeting and active targeting with sensors are described on p. 184 of SR5. If you know that you’ve been locked (or suspect it), you can to try to break it. Choose an enemy that has (or you think has) a lock on you, and make the Opposed Test. For every net hit, you reduce the target’s lock on you by one hit. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.

Simple Action against an enemy that has (or may have) a sensor lock on you: each net hit removes 1 hit from their lock. Your RCC's Noise Reduction rating adds to the pool.

R5 p. 30
SR5.MatrixActionBruteForce_GE:
You can use this action to mark a target without obtaining the normal permissions you need. This is the action for hackers emphasizing their Attack over their Sleaze, making it related to Hack on the Fly.

If you wish, you may also inflict 1 DV of Matrix damage to the target for every two full net hits, if the target can take Matrix damage, which is resisted with the target’s Device Rating + Firewall.

Places a mark without permission, relying on Attack (the counterpart of Hack on the Fly). Optionally, 1 DV of Matrix damage per 2 full net hits, resisted with Device Rating + Firewall.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionCalibration_GE:
You can increase the current Initiative Score of a number of personas on whom you have marks by 1 for every 2 hits. The number of personas affected cannot exceed your Data Processing. The Initiative Score then decreases each Combat Turn as normal.

Simple Action: each 2 hits add 1 to the current Initiative Score of personas you have a mark on, up to your Data Processing in number. The score then drops each Combat Turn as usual.

KC p. 37
SR5.MatrixActionChangeIcon_GE:
You change the target’s icon to one that you have a copy of or have designed yourself. Changing an icon doesn’t change the results of a Matrix Perception action, but might fool personas who don’t take the time to inspect your new look. You can target your own icon, if you like.

Simple Action, owner: gives the target icon (your own included) a look you designed or copied. Matrix Perception sees through it; a quick glance may not.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionRedefineOwnershipSuccess: Ownership redefined: the device reboots, its owner is ejected, and the AI suffers -2 to all actions for {depth} turn(s)
SR5.MatrixActionEmulateRating: Emulated rating (maximum {max}, added to the Overwatch Score)
SR5.MatrixActionEmulateLegal: Legal action (emulating raises no Overwatch Score)
SR5.MatrixActionCheckOverwatchScore_GE:
You find out how close the grid is to converging on you.

Simple Action: you learn your current Overwatch Score, meaning how close convergence is.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionConfusePilot_GE:
You send a stream of code to a device with a pilot (usually a drone, but sometimes an autonomous vehicle or gun emplacement) that resembles valid instructions but is in fact gobbledygook. If you succeed, the pilot becomes confused, and makes an immediate Simple Pilot x 2 Test to figure out what it’s going to do next (p. 269, SR5)—the threshold for this test is equal to half of your net hits. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction Rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.

Complex Action against a device with a Pilot (drone, autonomous vehicle, gun emplacement): on a success, it immediately rolls Pilot × 2 with a threshold of half your net hits to see what it does next. Your RCC's Noise Reduction adds to the pool.

R5 p. 30
SR5.MatrixActionControlDevice_GE:
You perform an action through a device you control (or at least control sufficiently), using your commlink or deck like a remote control or video-game controller.

You act through a device you control well enough, with your commlink or deck as a remote. Cost and test depend on the action performed.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionCrackFile_GE:
You remove the protection from a file, making it readable. This action doesn’t need to be performed on a file that isn’t protected, of course.

One mark needed: strips a file's protection so it can be read. Pointless on an unprotected file.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionCrashProgram_GE:
You overload part of your target’s memory and scramble one of its running programs.

You need to specify which program you’re trying to crash; you can learn what your target is running either with a Matrix Perception action or by observing the program in action. If you succeed, the program is scrambled: it ends and cannot be restarted until the device it was running on is rebooted.

One mark needed: pick a program the target is running, known through Matrix Perception or seen in use. On a success it stops and cannot restart until its device reboots.

SR5 p. 238
SR5.MatrixActionDataSpike_GE:
You send harmful instructions to a persona or device, causing Matrix damage to the target.

Matrix attack on a persona or device: DV = Attack + 1 per net hit + 2 per mark on the target, resisted with Device Rating + Firewall.

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionDenialOfService_GE:
A decker or technomancer may target a wirelessly active device or PAN. Make a Computer + Intuition [Data processing] Test opposed by Willpower + Firewall, and apply the number of net hits x 2 as a negative dice pool modifier to all tests made with that device until the beginning of the next Combat Turn. For every mark the decker or technomancer has on an enemy PAN, they may apply this effect to two additional devices slaved to the PAN..

Targets a wireless device or PAN: until the start of the next Combat Turn, every test made with the device takes −2 per net hit. Each mark on an enemy PAN extends the effect to two more slaved devices.

KC p. 37
SR5.MatrixActionDetectTargetLock_GE:
Passive targeting and active targeting with sensors are described on p. 184 of SR5. An active target lock sends wireless and other signals that hackers and riggers have learned to detect. The RCC, commlink, or deck that you’re using must be wireless-enabled to perform this action. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.

Free Action, owner: you detect an active sensor lock on you (threshold 2). Requires a wireless commlink, deck or RCC; the RCC's Noise Reduction adds to the pool.

R5 p. 30
SR5.MatrixActionDisarmDataBomb_GE:
You attempt to disarm a Data Bomb that you have detected (usually as the result of a Matrix Perception action). If you score any net hits, the Data Bomb is removed and deleted. If not, the Data Bomb activates, causing its damage and possibly destroying any file to which it was attached (assuming it was set to destroy the file).

Against a Data Bomb already spotted: at least 1 net hit deletes it; otherwise it goes off, deals its damage and may destroy its file.

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionEditFile_GE:
Edit File allows you to create, change, copy, delete, or protect any kind of file. The defender against this test is either the host holding the file or the owner of the file (if it’s not on a host). Each action is enough to alter one detail of a file—a short paragraph of text, a single detail of an image, or two or three seconds of video or audio

If you want to perform a continuous edit, such as removing your teammates from a video feed, you need to perform this action once per Combat Turn for as long as you want to keep the edit going.

If you use this action to copy a file, you are the new file’s owner. If the file you want to copy has protection on it, this action automatically fails. If the file has a Data Bomb, the Data Bomb goes off on you (so try to remember to scan files before you open them).

One mark needed: create, change, copy, delete or protect a file, one detail per action (a few lines, one image element, 2 or 3 seconds of audio or video). A running edit must be repeated each turn. Fails outright on a protected file; a Data Bomb on it goes off on you.

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionEnterOrExitHost_GE:
You enter a host that you have a mark on and your icon appears there, or you leave a host you’re already in. There is no test for this action: a host allows anyone to enter if they’ve got a mark, and anyone inside can exit. The host might not be so welcoming once you’re inside, of course, and some IC has the ability to keep you trapped in a host until you can break out.

No test: entering a host requires a mark on it, leaving requires nothing. Some IC can keep you from getting out.

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionEraseMark_GE:
You eradicate a mark that has been placed on your persona or on another icon.

Removes a mark placed on your persona or on another icon.

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionEraseMatrixSignature_GE:
You eradicate a Matrix signature that has been left by a Resonance being, such as a technomancer or a sprite.

Deletes the Matrix signature left behind by a Resonance being (technomancer, sprite).

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionFormatDevice_GE:
You rewrite the boot code for the device. The next time it would reboot, it instead shuts down for good, or until its software can be replaced.

A device that has been shut down in this fashion loses all of its wireless modifiers but can still be used as a normal mechanism (a door with a manual handle can be opened, a gun with a trigger can be fired, etc.) and cannot be accessed from the Matrix.

Three marks needed: at its next reboot, the device shuts down for good until its software is replaced. It loses its wireless bonuses and Matrix access but still works by hand (handle, trigger…).

SR5 p. 239
SR5.MatrixActionGarbageInGarbageOut_GE:
This allows a decker to “cross the wires” of a single device, confusing its input and output commands. Only a single input can be changed to correspond to a single output—devices can’t be reprogrammed wholesale or made to act in a manner outside of their original design through Garbage In/Garbage Out.

Three marks needed: swaps a single input command with a single output command on one device; it cannot be reprogrammed wholesale. The GM decides what can be swapped; a reboot puts everything back.

DT p. 178
SR5.MatrixActionGridHop_GE:
You hop to another grid—for example, you might jump from the public grid to Seattle’s Emerald City local grid. To do this, you must have access to your destination grid.

If you do not have access, you can use Brute Force or Hack on the Fly to hop to another grid illegally. If you’re inside a host, you need to leave the host before you can hop to another grid.

No test: you move to a grid you have access to. Without access, use Brute Force or Hack on the Fly. Not possible from inside a host.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionHackOnTheFly_GE:
You can use this action to mark a target without getting the normal permissions. This is the action for hackers emphasizing their Sleaze over their Attack, making it an analog to Brute Force.

Additionally, every two full net hits counts as one hit on a Matrix Perception Test, so you can get some info along with your mark.

Places a mark without permission, relying on Sleaze (the counterpart of Brute Force). Each 2 full net hits also count as 1 hit of Matrix Perception on the target.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionHaywire_GE:
Target must be a persona not running in VR. Haywire disables all of the target’s PAN-related functions. Physical devices still function, so smartguns can still fire and chemsuits still offer protection, but without wireless or PAN functions. This effect lasts until the target succeeds an extended Computer + Logic [Data Processing] (Hacker’s Net Hits, Simple Action) test with a threshold equal to the net hits from the attacker’s roll; each attempt takes a simple action. The target may simply reset their device and reboot it with a Complex Action; the device will be back online at the end of the following Combat Turn, which takes one minute. Glitching the test to fix the device adds an additional net hit to the attacker’s roll. A critical glitch causes all the devices on the PAN to require an OS reinstall. This takes multiple hours and a connection to a persona-enabled device.

Against a persona not in VR: all of the target's wireless and PAN functions stop (hardware still works by hand). They recover with an extended Computer + Logic [Data Processing] test, threshold = your net hits, one Simple Action per try, or by rebooting. A glitch adds 1 net hit to the attacker; a critical glitch forces a reinstall of the whole PAN.

KC p. 38
SR5.MatrixActionHide_GE:
You’ll probably be spotted by another icon, even if you’re running silent. You can use this action to make a target lose you. If you succeed, the target stops spotting you and needs to perform a new Matrix Perception action against you if it wants to find you again. You can’t hide from an icon that has a mark on you, so you’ll need to clear those before you can try this action.

You slip away from an icon that spotted you: it needs a new Matrix Perception to find you. Not possible if it has a mark on you.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionIAmTheFirewall_GE:
I Am the Firewall allows the hacker to give a Defense test bonus to all allies with access to an AR feed from the user. The number of bonus dice is equal to the number of hits on a Computer + Intuition [Data Processing] Test. This bonus lasts until the beginning of the hacker’s next Initiative Pass. The hacker can only share their feed with a number of users equal to or less than their Data Processing attribute.

When you take this action as an Interrupt Action, your Initiative Score is reduced by 5.

Complex Action (or Interrupt at −5 Initiative): your hits add as dice to the Defense tests of allies who receive your AR feed, up to your Data Processing in number, until your next Initiative Pass.

KC p. 38
SR5.MatrixActionIntervene_GE:
This allows the hacker to give an immediate defense bonus to the owner of a device slaved to the hacker’s PAN. This action can be taken only if the device making the attack is wirelessly enabled and the hacker is aware of it. When you take this action, your Initiative Score is reduced by 5. Roll your Computer + Intuition [Data Processing], adding the number of hits to your ally’s Defense test. This bonus applies only to the current Defense test—it cannot be carried over to any other Combat Turn or Initiative Pass.

Interrupt Action (−5 Initiative), if the attacking device is wireless and you are aware of it: your hits add to the Defense test of the owner of a device slaved to your PAN, for that defense only.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionInterveneEffectNotificat: receives {hits}D on their next Defense test.
SR5.WARN_MatrixSupportNoTarget: Target the allies receiving the effect (or select their token).
SR5.WARN_IAmTheFirewallTooManyTargets: {actor} can only share the AR feed with {max} users (Data Processing): {count} targeted.
SR5.WARN_InterveneSingleTarget: Intervene protects a single ally: target only one.
SR5.MatrixActionInviteMark_GE:
If you’re the owner of a device, file, persona, host, or IC program, you can offer other icons the opportunity to put a mark on your device, file, etc. When you make the offer, you choose the number of marks allowed, their duration, and how long the offer stands. The invitee can then mark your icon with a Free Action. You may revoke your offer at any time before the mark is placed, but once another icon has a mark, you need to either use the Erase Mark action or reboot your device to remove it before the duration you chose expires.

Owner, no test: you allow an icon to mark yours, setting how many marks, their duration and how long the offer lasts. The invitee marks with a Free Action. The offer can be withdrawn until taken; after that, use Erase Mark or reboot.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionJackOut_GE:
This jacks you out of the Matrix and reboots the device you are using. You suffer dumpshock if you were in VR.

You can only jack out yourself. You can’t dump other people except by beating them into submission through Matrix damage.

Simple Action: you leave the Matrix and your device reboots; dumpshock if you were in VR. Works only on yourself; if link-locked, a test is needed.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionJamSignals_GE:
This action turns the wireless device you are using into a local jammer.

As long as you do not use the device for any further Matrix actions, the device adds any hits you get on the test to the noise rating for all Matrix actions conducted by or targeting any devices within 100 meters.

Owner: your wireless device becomes a jammer. As long as it is used for no other Matrix action, your hits add to the Noise of every Matrix action made by or against a device within 100 m.

SR5 p. 240
SR5.MatrixActionJumpIntoRiggedDevice_GE:
You jump into a device that has a rigger adaptation, usually a vehicle or a drone. There’s a list of things you need to have in order to jump into a device: you have to have three marks on the device you want to jump into, you have to be in VR, the device you want to jump into has to have a rigger adaptation, and you have to have a control rig. If you are the device’s owner, or the device’s owner has given you permission to jump into the device, you don’t need to make a test. In the Matrix, the icon of the device you jumped into becomes part of your persona.

If someone else is already jumped into the device, you cannot attempt this action until he or she vacates.

Three marks, VR, a control rig and a rigger-adapted device are needed: you jump into the vehicle or drone. No test for the owner or someone with their permission. Its icon joins your persona. Only one person jumped in at a time.

SR5 p. 241
SR5.MatrixActionLoadProgram_GE:
Free Action: loads a program into a free slot.

SR5 p. 228
SR5.MatrixActionMasquerade_GE:
This action allows a hacker to impersonate a persona on the Matrix. Since persona data is updated in real time, this action requires 2 marks on one target (the persona being impersonated) and 2 marks on a second target (the icon you are trying to fool). For every net hit scored on a Hacking + Intuition [Sleaze] v. Logic + Firewall against the second target, you have convinced them you are target one for one minute. This can be used to impersonate someone online, intercept their calls, use their social media, rummage through their email history, or other creative mischief, but processes like changing device owners or performing major financial actions (like bank transfers) have too many double-checks for Masquerade to work. If the persona you’re impersonating logs off, those marks are immediately lost, and the disguise drops. While masquerading, you are never considered the owner with regard to any of the impersonated persona’s devices.

Two marks on the persona you copy and two on the icon you fool: each net hit convinces it for one minute that you are the other one (calls, mail, social feeds…). No effect on ownership changes or bank transfers; you never count as owner of their devices. If the copied persona logs off, the marks are lost.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionMatrixPerception_GE:
This versatile and important action is used both for finding icons in the Matrix and for analyzing Matrix objects. When you use this action to analyze a Matrix object or scan the vicinity for silent-running icons.

For each net hit scored, you can ask for one piece of information about the object—this could be type, a rating, how many marks it has on it, any files it may be carrying, which grid it is using, whether any silent running icons are in the area, or any other pertinent Matrix information. You learn one fact per net hit.

Finds icons or analyzes a Matrix object: each net hit answers one question (type, rating, marks on it, files, grid, silent-running icons nearby…).

SR5 p. 241
SR5.MatrixActionMatrixSearch_GE:
CYou search the Matrix for information about a topic. The time it takes and the threshold of the test depend on the general availability of the information in question and the area being searched, respectively. Any hits above and beyond the threshold can be used to reduce the search time. Divide the base time by the net hits to determine the reduction. If you fail this test, you still spend the full base time looking.

Information search: threshold and base time depend on the topic and the area searched. The time is divided by hits beyond the threshold; on a failure, the full time is spent.

SR5 p. 241
SR5.MatrixActionPopupCybercombat_GE:
Target must be a persona not running in VR. If the target has wireless-enabled AR, they are flooded with Matrix spam, taking a penalty to all actions equal to [net hits] until the start of the attacker’s next Combat Turn. If the attacker uses Cybercombat + Logic, the attack also deals Matrix damage equal to net hits.

Against a persona not in VR using wireless AR: penalty equal to net hits on all their actions until the start of your next Combat Turn. Cybercombat version: also deals that much Matrix damage.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionPopupHacking_GE:
Target must be a persona not running in VR. If the target has wireless-enabled AR, they are flooded with Matrix spam, taking a penalty to all actions equal to [net hits] until the start of the attacker’s next Combat Turn. If the attacker uses Hacking + Logic, they may immediately act as if the net hits on the attack were net hits on a Matrix Perception test, and they gain any relevant information.

Against a persona not in VR using wireless AR: penalty equal to net hits on all their actions until the start of your next Combat Turn. Hacking version: net hits also count as a Matrix Perception on the target.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionRebootDevice_GE:
The device on which this action is performed shuts down and immediately reboots. The device comes back online at the end of the following Combat Turn. The device ceases electronic functions and disappears from the Matrix until its reboot time is over.

This action only works on devices. It doesn’t work on hosts, living beings (like technomancers, although they can “reboot” themselves, p. 251), or Resonance constructs (like sprites), and the only persona it works on is your own. If you’re the owner of the device you’re rebooting, you don’t have to make a test. You can’t use this action on a device that is link-locked (p. 229).

Three marks (no test for the owner): the device shuts down and comes back at the end of the next Combat Turn, off the Matrix meanwhile. Persona: OS reset to 0, marks wiped; dumpshock in VR. Not hosts, living beings or sprites; not possible while link-locked.

SR5 p. 242
SR5.MatrixActionSendMessage_GE:
You send a text or audio message the length of a short sentence, an image, or a file via the Matrix to a user whose commcode you have. If you’re using the Matrix through a DNI, even if you’re in AR, you can send longer and more complicated messages, about a paragraph worth of text. You can also use this action to open a live feed to one or more recipients, using any digital recording devices you have.

One mark needed, no test: sends a sentence, an image or a file to a known commcode (a paragraph through DNI), or opens a live feed to one or more recipients.

SR5 p. 242
SR5.MatrixActionSetDataBomb_GE:
You set a Data Bomb in a file. When you do, choose the rating of the Data Bomb, up to the net hits on your test. You also need to choose whether or not the Data Bomb will delete the file to which it is attached when activated, and you need to program the passcode required to deactivate it. A file can only have one Data Bomb on it at a time.

The Data Bomb is triggered when someone attempts to read, edit, copy, protect, delete, or put another Data Bomb on the file without using the already-in-place Data Bomb’s passcode. When a Data Bomb goes off, it causes (Rating)D6 Matrix Damage (resisted normally) to the icon that tripped it, deletes the file (if it was set that way), and then is itself deleted. If the passcode is used, the Data Bomb doesn’t activate. Instead, it remains attached to the file, waiting for the next guy.

A Data Bomb can be detected using Matrix Perception. If it’s detected, it can be defused with the Disarm Data Bomb action; a disarmed Data Bomb is deleted. Damn.

One mark needed: traps a file with a bomb of chosen rating, up to your net hits, with a passcode, deciding whether it deletes the file. One per file. It goes off on anyone handling the file without the passcode: (Rating)D6 Matrix damage, then deletes itself. Can be found with Matrix Perception.

SR5 p. 242
SR5.MatrixActionSnoop_GE:
This action lets you intercept Matrix traffic sent to and from your target for as long as you have the target marked. You can listen to, view, or read this data live, or you can save it for later playback/viewing if you have something to store it on (your deck will do).

One mark needed: as long as the mark holds, you intercept the target's Matrix traffic, live or recorded if you have storage.

SR5 p. 242
SR5.MatrixActionSpoofCommand_GE:
You spoof a device’s owner’s identity, making the device think that your command is a legitimate one from its owner. You need one mark on the icon you are imitating; you do not need a mark on the target. The opposing dice roll is still based on the target, though. This trick only works on devices and agents, not IC, sprites, hosts, personas, or any other icons.

One mark on the icon you imitate, none on the target: the target device or agent takes your command as its owner's. No effect on IC, sprites, hosts or personas.

SR5 p. 242
SR5.MatrixActionSquelch_GE:
A successful Squelch test prevents the target device from calling or sending messages for a number of minutes equal to the net hits scored.

Simple Action: the target device cannot call or send messages for as many minutes as net hits.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionSubvertInfrastructure_GE:
This action allows a decker or technomancer to slightly alter the operation of multiple physical devices so they respond to the hacker’s commands. If the hacker has at least 1 mark on the host, a successful Electronic Warfare + Intuition [Sleaze] v. Intuition + Firewall Test allows them to control one similar simple device (traffic lights, vending machines, home appliances, desk lamps, etc., at gamemaster discretion) slaved to that host for every net hit. This action cannot be used to make an attack. The hacker can sustain controlling these devices as a Complex Action each Combat Turn.

One mark on the host: each net hit puts one simple device slaved to that host under your control (traffic lights, vending machines, appliances… GM's call), all of one kind. Never for attacks; keeping control costs a Complex Action each turn.

KC p. 39
SR5.MatrixActionSuppressNoise_GE:
As described on p. 268, SR5, this action allows riggers to use their RCC to reduce noise between themselves and their vehicles or drones. Reduce noise by the hits on this test, cumulative with any other forms of noise reduction. This effect lasts for the remainder of the current Combat Turn. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.

Complex Action, owner: your hits cut the Noise between you and your drones or vehicles until the end of the turn, on top of other reductions. The RCC's Noise Reduction adds to the pool.

R5 p. 30
SR5.MatrixActionSwapTwoPrograms_GE:
Swaps a running program for one in storage.

SR5 p. 228
SR5.MatrixActionSwitchInterfaceMode_GE:
You switch your perception from AR to VR or vice versa. Switching to VR causes your body to go limp, so don’t do it somewhere dangerous.

Simple Action: switches from AR to VR or back. In VR, your body goes limp.

SR5 p. 243
SR5.MatrixActionSwitchTwoMatrixAttribute:
Free Action: swaps two Matrix attributes on your deck.

SR5 p. 228
SR5.MatrixActionTag_GE:
The hacker may “tag” a number of targets on a single PAN, equal to their net hits, within their line of sight. They can then relay those tags wirelessly to allies. Tagging a target negates up to 2 dice in penalties from Visibility and Light/Glare to any affected ranged attack rolls allies may be making against that target, including blind-fire due to invisibility or shooting through cover. Allies who can see a tag may also take one additional Take Aim Action against that target as a Free Action on each Initiative Pass.

Tags may be sustained by spending a Simple Action to refresh the tags each Combat Turn. When using a PI-Tac, the hacker may add the PITac’s level to the number of targets they may tag. Note: In order for allies to receive this bonus, they must have the ability to see AROs.

Simple Action: tag as many targets in sight on one PAN as net hits (+ PI-Tac level). Allies who see AROs ignore up to 2 dice of visibility and light penalties on ranged attacks against them and get one free Take Aim per pass. A Simple Action each turn keeps them up.

KC p. 40
SR5.MatrixActionTargetDevice_GE:
Pick a wireless-enabled device you’ve spotted on the Matrix. You can target that device and feed targeting data to any pilot program or person with a Sensor rating or smartlink that is slaved to your RCC. For the rest of the Combat Turn, the slaved attackers receive a dice pool bonus equal to your net hits when targeting the device you’re tracking for them. Your RCC’s Noise Reduction rating is added as a dice pool bonus for this action.

Complex Action on a wireless device you spotted: until the end of the turn, pilots and smartlink or sensor users slaved to your RCC gain dice equal to your net hits to attack it. The RCC's Noise Reduction adds to the pool.

R5 p. 30
SR5.MatrixActionTraceIcon_GE:
This action lets you look for the physical location of a device or a persona in the Matrix. On a success, the target's real position is found, and stays known as long as the character still has at least one mark on it.

This action does not work on hosts, since they usually have no physical presence, nor on IC programs, since they only exist on their host.

Two marks needed: you learn where a device or persona physically is, and keep knowing it while you still have a mark on it. No effect on hosts or IC.

SR5 p. 243
SR5.MatrixActionTrackback_GE:
You find the physical location of a device or persona in the Matrix. After succeeding with this action, you know the target’s location for as long as you have at least one mark on the target. This doesn’t work on hosts because they generally have no physical location, or IC programs because they are confined to their hosts.

Owner, on a grid only: follows a mark spotted on your device back to whoever placed it. Extended test, 30-minute interval, threshold 10 + that persona's Sleaze. If it runs silent, the trail ends near it.

DT p. 179
SR5.MatrixActionUnloadProgram_GE:
Unloads a program and frees its slot.

SR5 p. 228
SR5.MatrixActionWatchdog_GE:
Target must be a persona or device. If successful, place one mark on the target. The user is now aware of the Matrix actions the target is going to use before they use them, and they may attempt to stop them. A Watchdog mark allows the hacker to use Haywire or Popup as Interrupt Actions (for –10 initiative) or Squelch as an Interrupt Action (for –5 initiative) against the target with the Watchdog mark. This ability lasts as long as the target is marked by the user.

Places a mark on a persona or device: while it holds, you see its Matrix actions coming and can use Haywire or Popup against it as Interrupts (−10 Initiative) or Squelch (−5).

SR5.TransmutationConfirm: Remove {count} implant(s) from {name} and deal {damage} boxes of Physical damage?
SR5.RapidFireCasterRest_D: No use left today. Tick it if the character took eight hours of full rest: the uses come back and this one counts (Forbidden Arcana p. 39). The uses also come back by themselves a day of game time after the first one.
SR5.GuruParticipants_D: Ordinary participants who believe in your tradition: +1 die and +1 limit per (60 / Charisma), at most your Ritual Spellcasting rank (Forbidden Arcana p. 42).
SR5.BloodMagicPoints_D: Granted by the GM after a melee wound; lost after the following Combat Turn (Street Grimoire p. 90).
SR5.BloodMagicLeft_D: Those of your sacrifices, plus those your own wounds give (martyr magic).
SR5.BloodMartyrBoxes: Boxes you inflict on yourself (martyr magic)
SR5.BloodMartyrBoxes_D: 3 Physical boxes = 1 point, with no addiction test, and your wound modifiers are ignored for this spell (Forbidden Arcana p. 135). Giger Spit, Pyrohemetics and Blood Whip: the first box gives the point.
SR5.BloodMagicSpent: Blood magic: Force +{force}, Magic for the Drain +{drainMagic}, Drain −{drain} ({martyr} of martyr magic)
SR5.WARN_BloodSpellNeedsPoint: A Blood spell is cast with at least 1 Blood Magic Point (Forbidden Arcana p. 125).

SR5.BloodSacrificeSpent: The points of this wound were already granted.
SR5.BloodSacrificeConfirm: {user} asks for {caster} the Blood Magic Points of the {boxes} box(es) dealt to {victim} — {kind}. Grant them?
SR5.BloodSacrificeRefused: The GM did not grant these Blood Magic Points to {caster}.
SR5.BloodSacrificeGranted: {caster} gains {points} Blood Magic Point(s) (total {total}), lost after the following Combat Turn.
SR5.AthamePoints_D: At most the athame's Force; half is lost 1 week, 1 month and 3 months after the Blood Rite, rounded towards the loss (Street Grimoire p. 90).
SR5.AthameStore_D: During a Blood Rite (Street Grimoire p. 91), run by the GM: the Blood Magic Points at hand go into the athame, at most its Force.
SR5.WARN_AthameNothingToStore: No active athame or no Blood Magic Point at hand.
SR5.WARN_AthameFull: This athame is full (at most its Force).
SR5.Cannibalize_D: 3 Blood Magic Points per point of physical attribute (you have {pool}), a Simple Action, up to the augmented maximum; lasts {duration} Combat Turns (Magic × initiate grade, Street Grimoire p. 90).
SR5.CannibalizeKarma: Spend as much Karma as attribute points: {duration} days

SR5.CannibalizeDoneDays: {adept} spends {points} Blood Magic Points and {raised} Karma (Cannibalize): {list}, for {duration} days. The effect stays on the sheet until the GM removes it.
SR5.WARN_CannibalizeNoPoints: Cannibalize needs at least 3 Blood Magic Points.
SR5.WARN_CannibalizeTooMany: It takes {cost} Blood Magic Points, you have {pool}.
SR5.NaniteAttributeBoost: Attribute Boost (head case): lasts as many turns as hits, then Stun damage
SR5.NaniteAmplification: Amplification (monad): +4 at most, lasts as many turns as hits, then 1 box past the natural maximum and Nanite Volume lowered for 1 minute
SR5.NaniteToxinResistance: Toxin Resistance (head case): adds the Nanite Volume
SR5.DisarmWeaponPenalty: {value} dice penalty to use the weapon on their next action phase
SR5.HELP_RiggerCabledMsg: Checked, the drone is linked to its rigger by a cable: its actions suffer no noise from distance (SR5 p. 266). Unchecked, under remote control or jumped in, every action of the drone suffers the noise of the distance between its token and the rigger's (p. 231: 1 from 101 m to 1 km, 3 up to 10 km…), less the rigger's Noise Reduction; a relay unit of the network measures from itself (Rigger 5.0 p. 168). If either token is not on the scene shown, nothing is counted: the gamemaster adds the noise by hand.

SR5.NotEnoughMarksOnTarget: The target does not have enough marks
SR5.NotEnoughMarksOnFile: Not enough marks on the file itself: a mark on the host that holds it does not count for its files. Hack the file on the fly to mark it (SR5 p. 239).
SR5.WARN_OwnerOnlyAction: {name}: only the owner of the icon may take this action (SR5 p. 237).
SR5.WARN_OwnerUnknown: owner-only action, but the system does not know who owns {name} (device with no master, drone with no creator): the action went through, yours to rule (SR5 p. 237).
SR5.GridHopHint: Grid Hop (complex action, SR5 p. 240): to a grid the character has access to (subscription, lifestyle, SR5 p. 234).
SR5.GridHopAccess: The character has access to this grid
SR5.GridHopIllegal: With no access, the hop is illegal: Hack on the Fly or Brute Force against the grid (SR5 p. 240), opposed by the GM. Nothing is spent.
SR5.WARN_GridHopInHost: No grid hop from inside a host: leave it first (SR5 p. 240).
SR5.DISEASE_IsPathogenHint: A toxin that comes back: incubation, then one test per interval (Run Faster p. 142)
SR5.DISEASE_InfectButton: Infect (selected tokens, or list of characters)
SR5.DISEASE_Volunteer: Willing subject (−{n} dice on the first test)
SR5.DISEASE_ReexposedRecovering: {names}: recovering from {name}, the new exposure is not applied (the book says nothing of it). Your call; you may infect again once the recovery is over.
SR5.DISEASE_NoTarget: Tick at least one character to infect.
SR5.DISEASE_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the disease ledger.
SR5.DISEASE_DueFirst: {actor}: incubation of {name} over, first resistance test
SR5.DISEASE_TreatHint: Net hits of the Heal Disease spell (SR5 p. 288), a bonus until the disease ends
SR5.DISEASE_RequestGone: This test was already applied, or the GM asked for another one.
SR5.DISEASE_ZeroReached: An attribute or the Essence is down to 0: death or incapacity as the disease says, for the GM to rule.
SR5.DISEASE_CardPool: The card says: {hits} hits on {pool} dice.
SR5.DISEASE_HitsAbovePool: More hits than dice: the card was edited.
SR5.DISEASE_HitsOnDice: The card's dice show {hits} hits: the card was edited.

SR5.DISEASE_HitsAboveCeiling: The card's dice show {hits} hits, more than the pool and Edge ({pool}): exploding sixes can do it, but the card may have been edited. Type the hits yourself.
SR5.DISEASE_Recovering: Disease beaten: {n} Essence to recover, 1 every 24 hours.

SR5.DISEASE_MemoryLoss: Memory loss: memory test (threshold {threshold}) to use a knowledge or recall the last 12 or 24 hours.
SR5.HardenedArmorHitsOnly: Hardened Armor: only its automatic hits on resistance (Granite skin)
SR5.HUNGER_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the hunger ledger.
SR5.HUNGER_Zero: {actor} has no Essence left: it dies on {date} unless it feeds.
SR5.HUNGER_Dead: {actor} did not feed in time: it dies (SR5 p. 401).
SR5.HUNGER_PowerUsed: {actor} used {power}: bring the next Essence loss one week closer?
SR5.INFECTION_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM keeps the infection ledger.
SR5.INFECTION_NotZero: Infection can only be tried on a victim whose Essence has fallen to 0 (SR5 p. 398).
SR5.INFECTION_AlreadyComa: This victim is already in the coma of the Infection.
SR5.INFECTION_NoCreature: No creature with the Infection power (and Essence Drain) in the scene or in the world.
SR5.INFECTION_Rule: Only if this creature's Essence Drain brought the victim to 0 (SR5 p. 398). Opposed test: Magic + Charisma of the creature against Body + Willpower of the victim. On a tie, the victim resists (general rule of combat, p. 172).
SR5.INFECTION_Infected: {victim} is infected by {creature} and falls into a coma. Wakes up on {date} as an Infected with 1 point of Essence.
SR5.INFECTION_Offer: The Essence of {victim} has fallen to 0 near a creature with the Infection power. If its Essence Drain emptied the victim: try the Infection?

SR5.INFECTION_Woken: Woken from the Infection: set Essence to 1 from the GM's card
SR5.INFECTION_VictimGone: The victim no longer exists (token or actor deleted): it leaves the infection ledger.

SR5.CFD_NanoScrubIVOnly: NanoScrub can only be given intravenously (Dark Terrors p. 83).
SR5.CFD_AerosolTooWeak: As an aerosol the Rating is halved (rounded down): at least 2 doses are needed.

SR5.CFD_OverwritersSpent: The Overwriters of {actor} are spent: the treatment fails.

SR5.HELP_MonadStrain: Lockdown (p. 202): the device attributes are mental attribute + Nanite Volume, and matrix damage becomes Stun. Original (Dark Terrors p. 84): the Monad is treated as an AI on its nanite swarm (rating and attributes = Nanite Volume), with two monitors, Core and swarm. Dark Terrors p. 87 leaves the choice to the GM.
SR5.HELP_MonadCoreMonitor: The Monad's "source code": 8 + Matrix Entity Concentration / 2. Its damage gives wound modifiers. Matrix damage goes to the swarm; only the GM puts it on the Core, with the button of the damage card (Dark Terrors p. 84).
SR5.MONAD_CoreRule: The matrix damage of an original strain Monad goes to its nanite swarm. The GM may put it on its Core instead, as for an AI (Dark Terrors p. 84, Data Trails p. 155). The suggested number comes from the card: check it.
SR5.MONAD_CoreFullRule: Dark Terrors p. 84: the Monad is dissipated. Its Nanite Volume drops by 1 + the overflow not resisted. It resists the overflow with Willpower + Firewall + Matrix Entity Concentration, as an AI does with its Depth (Data Trails p. 155; the book does not say). At 0 it is destroyed; otherwise it sleeps (10 - Nanite Volume) hours, at least 1.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmFullRule: Dark Terrors p. 84: the Monad is permanently destroyed. The host's current and maximum mental attributes (Logic, Intuition, Charisma, Willpower) drop by Nanite Volume / 4, rounded down. The Nanite Volume drops to 0.
SR5.MONAD_CorePool: Pool: Willpower {willpower} + Firewall {firewall} + Matrix Entity Concentration {cem}.
SR5.MONAD_SurplusFromPlayer: This Core was filled by a player or by hand: the overflow is unknown, type it.
SR5.MONAD_CoreResult: Resistance: {pool} dice, {hits} hits against an overflow of {surplus}. Nanite Volume -{loss}: {before} → {after}.
SR5.MONAD_Sleeps: The personality goes dormant for {hours} h while its source code recompiles.
SR5.MONAD_Destroyed: Nanite Volume at 0: the Monad is permanently destroyed.
SR5.MONAD_Ejected: Any other persona connected to its swarm is ejected and suffers dumpshock where relevant: the GM applies it.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmConfirm: Nanite Volume {volume}: each mental attribute of the host loses {loss} point(s) (never below 1), and the Nanite Volume drops to 0. Apply?
SR5.MONAD_SwarmResult: Swarm bricked (Nanite Volume {volume}): host's mental attributes -{loss}, Nanite Volume at 0.
SR5.MONAD_SwarmReminders: The system keeps no attribute maximum of the actor's own: note the lower maximums. The head case device stays on the sheet, for the GM to remove.
SR5.MONAD_ActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM resolves the dissipation or the destruction of a Monad.
SR5.MONAD_Gone: This Monad no longer exists or is no longer of the original strain.
SR5.MONAD_Formatted: Swarm formatted: the Monad repairs its boot sector with {actions} Complex Action(s), doing nothing else. If it reboots before, it is destroyed as by a Core overflow (Dark Terrors p. 85).
SR5.MONAD_CoreFromPlayer: This card was written by {user}, not by a GM: the suggested number, like the attack damage it shows, can be forged. Check it against the attack itself.
SR5.MONAD_StrainGMOnly: The CFD strain is the GM's choice (Dark Terrors p. 87): only a GM changes it.
SR5.MONAD_StrainUndone: {user} changed the CFD strain of {name}: put back, it is the GM's choice.
SR5.MONAD_CoreBound: At most {bound} box(es): the Attack of {name} plus its largest matrix action pool, read on its sheet (the most damage its attack can deal, Edge aside).
SR5.MONAD_CoreNoAttacker: Attacker not found: no box can be put on the Core from this card. Change the Core monitor by hand if needed.

SR5.DEFRAG_NoTechnomancer: No character of the world bears the Defragmentation echo.
SR5.DEFRAG_DialogIntro: Expel {target} from its host. It resists with {strength} × 2 dice; {strength} net hits are needed.
SR5.DEFRAG_Connection: A Matrix connection to the target is needed, or a device it can use as a residence (Dark Terrors p. 86).
SR5.DEFRAG_Expelled: Expelled: {target} leaves its host and escapes into the Matrix ({net} net hit{s}, {needed} needed).
SR5.DEFRAG_Failed: The Deactivation fails ({net} net hit{s}, {needed} needed).
SR5.DEFRAG_ExpelledAI: If the AI lived in its home device, it also loses it as its primary residence.
SR5.DEFRAG_PushRefused: (Push the Limit asked, but no Edge is left: refused)
SR5.DEFRAG_InProgress: This request is already being confirmed.

SR5.DEFRAG_Push: Push the Limit (1 point of Edge, spent when the GM confirms; {n} left)
SR5.DEFRAG_Waiting: Waiting for the GM, who counts again and confirms.

SR5.DEFRAG_ConfirmNote: The announced modifier is not taken over: type the one you keep. The hits kept never exceed the ones announced nor what the pool worked out allows. When the limit is pushed, the point of Edge is spent on confirming. The system then rolls the target's resistance.

SR5.SETTINGS_HungerMonth_T: Essence Loss: length of a lunar month (days)
SR5.SETTINGS_HungerMonth_D: An Infected loses 1 point of stolen Essence per lunar month (SR5 p. 401). The book gives no number of days: 29.5 by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_RevealDiseases_D: When ticked, the player also sees the Power and the number of tests of their character's disease. Unticked, they see only its name and what they feel, and nothing during the incubation.
SR5.PerceptionModSpecificallyLooking: Perceiver is specifically looking/listening for it

SR5.PORTRAIT_OptimalSize: Optimal picture size is 288 pixels wide by 288 pixels high.
SR5.PreparationFullPotency_D: Hours the preparation keeps its full Potency before losing it (SR5 p. 305): Potency × 2; × 3 with Durable Preparations or for a Godi (Forbidden Arcana p. 36, 68); × 4 for the Islamic alchemist practitioner or with the Sacrifice of blood magic (p. 39, 132). Only the longest counts. Set by the gamemaster.
SR5.PreparationDecayRate_D: After the full time, the preparation loses 1 Potency, then 1 more every hour (SR5 p. 305), or every day with the Fixation metamagic (p. 325). A fovea, a dispersion circle or an alchera hasten it: the gamemaster lowers the Potency by hand. Set by the gamemaster.
SR5.HELP_SwarmNumber: Rigger 5.0 p. 31: the drones slaved to one RCC running the Swarm program, and carrying the same number, act as one drone with several bodies. 0: no swarm.
SR5.SwarmActive: Swarm {number}: {count} drones, +{bonus} to dice and limit
SR5.SwarmInactive_noProgram: Swarm {number} inactive: the RCC does not run the Swarm program
SR5.SwarmInactive_alone: Swarm {number} inactive: fewer than two drones (slaved, working, on the scene)
SR5.SwarmInactive_notMember: Swarm {number} inactive for this drone: destroyed, bricked, not slaved or off the scene
SR5.RammingAngleHint: From the rear: difference between the Speeds; on the side: the ramming vehicle's Speed; head-on: both Speeds added. It takes half the damage (rounded up) from the rear or the side, all of it head-on (Rigger 5 p. 177).
SR5.RammingLocomotionHint: Speed is multiplied by locomotion before the table: watercraft ×0.8, ground ×1, rotorcraft ×3, jet ×4 (Rigger 5 p. 181). Vector thrust ×3 and airship ×1 are a table ruling, the book is silent. Rounded to the nearest, at least 1 when the vehicle moves.
SR5.RammingGaitHint: Against a pedestrian or an object: the target must be within the vehicle's walking or running range, -3 dice when running (SR5 p. 203). The gait fills in the relative speed from the vehicle's Speed; the GM may correct it.
SR5.RammingRelativeSpeedHint: Relative speed in meters per turn, for the Collision Damage table (SR5 p. 203-204).
SR5.RangeWithEnvironment_D: Range is an environmental modifier (SR5 p. 175): only the worst condition counts, one row further when several are equally severe. This line gives what range adds to the Environment line.
SR5.HELP_OrichalcumEditMsg: Left click: −1, right click: +1. Orichalcum replaces any reagent; its uses stay in the GM's hands (Street Grimoire p. 209-210, Forbidden Arcana p. 192).
SR5.ReagentForeignHint: Another tradition's reagents work at only half their Power (SR5 p. 317).
SR5.ReagentHarvestZoneHint: An hour of astral perception, then Alchemy + Magic [Mental] (SR5 p. 317). Overharvested area: Forbidden Arcana p. 187.
SR5.ReagentHarvestZone_tradition: Suited to my tradition (1 drachm / 2 hits)
SR5.SETTINGS_ReagentSystem_D: Core rulebook: a single stock of drachms. Shadow Spells: raw, refined, radical reagents and orichalcum, refining. Forbidden Arcana: the same, each tier also giving a limit and Drain bonus.
SR5.WARN_BindingReagents: Binding needs {reagents} drachms of reagents (SR5 p. 300).
SR5.RitualCircleLeader: Leader: {name}. Participants announce themselves before the sealing.
SR5.RitualCircleSealed: The leader seals the ritual: no one can join anymore.
SR5.RitualAssistNoSkill: Without the Ritual Spellcasting skill, no die to add; the Drain is still taken.
SR5.RitualAssistOtherTradition: Tradition different from the leader's: -2 dice.
SR5.RitualAssistGlitch: Glitch: this participant does not raise the leader's limit.
SR5.RitualAssistCriticalGlitch: Critical glitch: no participant raises the leader's limit.
SR5.SceneBackgroundCountMsg: Configure Background Count for this scene
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint: Aetherology p. 32-34: fills the rating and alignment, which you may then change within the book's range.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_astralRift: Astral rift (AETH p. 32-33): mundanes may project; uninitiated pass without the Dweller on the Threshold. A mundane whose body leaves the rift, or whose rift closes, fades after [Essence] hours.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_astralShallows: Astral shallows (AETH p. 33): switching to astral perception is a Free Action; mundanes see the astral without touching it.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theMist: The Mist (AETH p. 33), Force 3 to 10: noise + Force (applied); Force as a penalty to ranged attacks and Perception; Confusion (Magic = Force x 2); Movement; +2 Composure threshold, one test per hour; -1 to spirits' tests, which try to flee; rifts from 6.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_daoineannDraoidheil: Daoineann Draoidheil (AETH p. 33), Force 8 to 12, druidic: fixed mana storm; every spell and triggered preparation scatters randomly.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_fovea: Fovea (AETH p. 33-34), ebb 7 to 12: preparations lose 1 Potency every 30 min (6 h if anchored); the fovea loses 1 Force every 2 h and fades below 4.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_mayaCloud: Maya Cloud (AETH p. 34), Force 14 to 16: noise + Force (applied); Force as a penalty to Perception in and through the cloud.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theVeil: The Veil (AETH p. 34), Force 12 to 14: sustains a Chaotic World spell at its Force; crossing without electronic navigation exits elsewhere.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_theVoid: The Void (AETH p. 34), ebb 13 to 20: reagents are drained; a focus left more than [Force] hours is destroyed.
SR5.BGPhenomenonHint_manaStorm: Mana storm (AETH p. 33): see Street Grimoire p. 36; enter its Force.
SR5.ManaShiftApply_flux: Apply Mana Flux to the scene (+1, {hours} h)
SR5.ManaShiftApply_ebb: Apply Mana Ebb to the scene (−1, {hours} h)

SR5.ManaShiftApplied_ebb: Mana Ebb: the background count of "{scene}" drops by 1 for {hours} h.

SR5.ManaShiftFails_ebb: Mana Ebb fails: it only succeeds on a positive background count (here {count}). The Drain is still resisted (Shadow Spells p. 22).
SR5.ManaShiftGMOnly: Only the GM applies a ritual to the scene's background count.
SR5.ManaShiftNoScene: No scene to apply the ritual to.
SR5.ManaShiftCardRefused: Ritual card refused: it was not rolled by a GM, or it is not the resistance of a Mana Flux / Mana Ebb.
SR5.ManaShiftActiveGMOnly: Only the active GM applies a ritual: their browser keeps the ledger of spent cards.
SR5.ManaShiftAlreadyApplied: This ritual card has already been applied.
SR5.ManaShiftConfirm: Apply {name} (Force {force}) to the scene {scene}: background count shifted by 1 for {hours} hours?
SR5.ManaShiftHint: Shadow Spells p. 22: each one moves the count by 1 toward 0 for [Force] hours of game time, never past 0. A ritual that has run out goes away when game time passes.

SR5.ToxinEffectManasphereCut_GE:
Better Than Bad p. 141: no magic of any kind (Magic brought to 0: no spell, adept powers off) for [12 − (Body or Magic, the higher)] hours, at least 1 hour. A dual-natured being also takes −4 dice to every action. Over 24 hours of continuous exposure: mutations, then death.

No magic at all (Magic at 0: no spells, no adept powers) for 12 − (Body or Magic, the higher) hours, 1 minimum. A dual-natured being also takes −4 dice on everything. Continuous exposure past 24 h: mutations, then death.

Better Than Bad p. 157
SR5.ToxinBlightSpecial: Only affects the Awakened and dual-natured beings.
SR5.ToxinBlightDmsoSpecial: An Awakened resists with their Drain resistance instead of toxin resistance, and the damage is Stun Drain. A spirit exposed loses its Immunity to Normal Weapons against this damage.

SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumBaseWeapons_D: Compendium searched for the base weapons given to new actors (spirit natural attacks, unarmed strike...). Items are recognized by their system effects (baseOwnItem), not by their name.
SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumCreaturePowers_D: Compendium searched for the base and optional powers of spirits. Items are recognized by their system effects (spiritPower), not by their name. A power is given once, even when the compendium holds it twice.
SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumExtra_D: Your custom compendiums, read after the compendium above (or after the official ones in "Automatic"). They add items recognized by the same system effects; a power already found in the main compendium is not given twice.
SR5.SETTINGS_CompendiumSpritePowers_D: Compendium searched for the base and optional powers of sprites. Items are recognized by their system effects (baseOwnItem, spritePower), not by their name.
SR5.SETTINGS_CyberEyesReplaceNaturalVisi: A character wearing cybereyes loses the vision its metatype gave it, unless it bought that vision again as an enhancement: this is the rule (SR5 p. 94). Uncheck it only if your table chooses to keep both.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevLogActive_D: Display Shadowrun 5 system development messages in the browser/app console.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevLogLevel_D: Filtering level of displayed development messages.
SR5.SETTINGS_DevicelessAILogicDefense_D: An AI outside any device defends against Matrix actions with its Willpower or Intuition alone, depending on the action (Data Trails p. 152), with no Matrix attribute. The book does not say which one replaces Logic when the defense calls for it: this setting picks it. Defenses using Willpower or Intuition keep them. The same attribute resists Matrix damage, for which the book gives no pool without a device or Firewall (Data Trails p. 152 and 155).
SR5.SETTINGS_DevicelessAILogicDefense_T: AI outside a device: attribute replacing Logic in defense and resistance
SR5.SETTINGS_EmulateOverwatchHalf_D: By the book, an illegal Emulate adds its rating to the AI's Overwatch Score, or its hits when Edge pushes the limit (Data Trails p. 154). Checked, it adds half of that, rounded up. Unchecked: the book's rule.
SR5.SETTINGS_EmulateOverwatchHalf_T: AI Emulate: half the rating to the Overwatch Score (house rule)
SR5.SETTINGS_HomunculusMaterialArmor_D: The book (SR5 p. 298) gives a homunculus the Structure of its material as Body, and no Armor. Checked, it also gets the Armor of that material (Barrier Ratings table, SR5 p. 197).
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_D: What bounds an augmented physical or mental attribute (cyberware, bioware, magic). The book: +4 at most over the natural rating (SR5 p. 94). The excess is removed, and the attribute's tooltip shows the real and the kept values. Magic, Resonance and Edge are not concerned. "No cap" lifts this cap but keeps the bound of the spells and adept powers that raise an attribute: the metatype augmented maximum (SR5 p. 288 and 309).
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_bonus: +4 at most over the natural rating (book, SR5 p. 94)
SR5.SETTINGS_AugmentationCap_augmentedMa: Augmented maximum only: metatype maximum + 4 (SR5 p. 66, 288, 309)
SR5.AugmentationCapReason_boost: spell or adept power bounded by the augmented maximum, SR5 p. 288 and 309
SR5.AugmentationCapUnknownMetatype: Cap: metatype unknown to the table (SR5 p. 66), no cap applied
SR5.SETTINGS_FreeReload_T: Reload without spending an action (house rule)
SR5.SETTINGS_FreeReload_D: The book has reloading cost actions (SR5 p. 164 and table p. 163). Checked, reloading in combat costs no action when the right rounds are in the inventory, and a full refill becomes possible. Ejecting a clip alone keeps its cost.
SR5.SETTINGS_MentorMask_T: Mask of the mentor (Forbidden Arcana p. 182)
SR5.SETTINGS_MentorMask_D: Optional rule: a magician reduces all their Drain by 1 (never below 2), an adept gains 1 Power Point.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpiritLeash_D: Optional rule: a tight leash counts as a sustained spell (−2), and a spirit scoring 6 − (Force / 2) hits or more offers the gamemaster a leash test.
SR5.SpiritElemental_D: Elemental trait (Forbidden Arcana p. 181): mental attributes lowered by Force / 2 (minimum 1), one more service when summoned or bound, never tests the leash.
SR5.SpiritWild_D: Wild spirit (Forbidden Arcana p. 176-179): cannot be summoned; banished against Force × 2, net hits adding up to Force × 2.
SR5.SpiritDomain_D: Domain trait (Forbidden Arcana p. 179): Magic × 2 for Accident, Guard and Search.
SR5.SpiritFree_D: Free spirit (SR5 p. 304, Street Grimoire p. 203): the only spirit with Edge of its own. It spends it itself; it spends its former summoner's only under a magic pact.
SR5.SpiritFreeEdge_D: Edge of the free spirit. Empty: Force / 2, rounded up (SR5 p. 304 and p. 48). Street Grimoire (p. 203) has it start at 1 and grow in play: type it here.
SR5.SpiritMagicPact_D: Magic pact of a free spirit (Street Grimoire p. 137): the free spirit may spend the Edge of the character who summoned it. A summoned or bound spirit needs none: its summoner may always spend his Edge on its tests (SR5 p. 304).
SR5.AstralReputationAdjustment_D: Added to the reputation from the index: +6 for the hermetic elementalist (Forbidden Arcana p. 181), −1 per conjuring geas, atonement (Street Grimoire p. 207).
SR5.HermeticElementalist_D: Forbidden Arcana p. 181: their air, water, fire and earth spirits take the Elemental trait (lower mental attributes, easier binding). Apply the +6 adjustment.
SR5.WARN_SpiritBondsGMOnly: Indexes, reputations and spirit traits are written by the gamemaster only.
SR5.WARN_SpiritForceUnknownDrain: Spirit not found (token on another scene?): its Force cannot be compared with the Magic, the drain is counted as stun. If it exceeds the Magic, the drain is physical: the gamemaster fixes it by hand.

Modification Points: the optional rule of Rigger 5.0 p. 122-124, one pool equal to the Body, +1 for free, Armor beyond 3 × Body slows the drone down. Vehicles always keep their slots.

Unchecked: core rulebook.
SR5.SETTINGS_BBAdvancedMedkits_D: Optional rules of Bullets & Bandages p. 16-19: the medkit rating is only bonus dice, its supplies (charges) go down by one per patient, and an empty medkit brings back the -3 penalty. Unchecked: core rulebook.

Success: +2 dice on the next stabilization or treatment test, +1 on a glitch, -2 on a critical glitch.
SR5.BB_DiagnoseResult: Diagnosis of {name}: {bonus} dice on the next care.
SR5.BB_MedkitEmpty: The medkit has no supplies left: -3 penalty (Bullets & Bandages p. 18).

SR5.SETTINGS_LowLightGreenTint_D: Night-vision goggles green tint on what a token using low-light vision sees. A visual convention, not a rule: the book only says low-light vision lets one see normally in dim light (SR5 p. 444). Off, the token sees in natural colours. The tint only shows while a single token is selected (a Foundry limit).

SR5.SpriteCompanionDescription:
Companion sprites are always by your side, right when you need them. They exist to protect and serve.

The bodyguard sprite: stays close to its technomancer to defend them (Computer, Electronic Warfare; Shield and Bodyguard powers).

KC p. 100
SR5.SpriteCourierDescription:
Courier sprites are great at delivering messages securely and are pretty good trackers.

The messenger sprite: carries data safely and can follow a trail through the Matrix.

SR5 p. 259
SR5.SpriteCrackDescription:
If you need a sprite for a quiet run that stays under the radar, the Crack sprite has what you need.

The infiltration sprite: useful when the run has to go unnoticed.

SR5 p. 259
SR5.SpriteDataDescription:
Data sprites are masters of finding and manipulating data. They make great librarians, searchbots, and trivia contest ringers.

Information specialist: finding, sorting and handling data.

SR5 p. 259
SR5.SpriteFaultDescription:
The Fault sprite is the one you want to have your back in a fight. Cold as IC and twice as tenacious, they’ll shred your enemies in the blink of an icon.

The combat sprite: guards its technomancer and goes after Matrix enemies.

SR5 p. 259
SR5.SpriteGeneralistDescription:
Not particularly good at any one thing, but also not bad. They are what you make of them.

The all-rounder sprite, with no particular strength or weakness (Hacking, Computer, Electronic Warfare; two optional powers of your choice).

KC p. 100
SR5.SpriteMajorForm_D: Technoshaman (Kill Code p. 92): the sprite gets the major form power of its type; the fading of the compiling is doubled.
SR5.SpriteMajorFormUse: Using this power takes all the sprite's remaining tasks, and it decompiles as soon as it is done (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_freenet_D: The sprite spreads a file it has a mark on: each initiative pass, it copies it to as many devices, personas or hosts as its level, among those whose Firewall is lower than its Sleaze. While it sustains the power, its Overwatch Score rises by its Sleaze each combat turn (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_gatekeeper_D: The sprite picks a persona, the keymaster, and a host or a device. If its Sleaze equals or exceeds the target's Firewall, the keymaster counts as its owner. While it sustains the power, its Overwatch Score rises by its Sleaze each combat turn (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_supercomputer_D: For a single task tied to Data Processing, the sprite adds its level to its Data Processing, then 1 more each combat turn it sustains the power. Its Overwatch Score rises each turn by its Data Processing so modified (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_annihilation_D: Opposed test of Cybercombat + Resonance [Attack] against Intuition + Firewall. If it wins, the target resists matrix damage with a DV equal to the sprite's Resonance: physical for a technomancer, physical for a decker's device or a device; a host taking more boxes than its rating goes offline for as many hours (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_overdrive_D: With a mark on a device, the sprite raises all its ratings by 1, then 1 more each combat turn it sustains the power. When the bonus reaches three times one of the device's base ratings, the device breaks down and takes as much damage as the bonus (Kill Code p. 93).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_sacrifice_D: The sprite gives itself up for a persona: it heals its whole matrix condition monitor, gains half the sprite's level (rounded up) to all its matrix attributes for as many combat turns as the level, and takes no damage during the turn the power is used (Kill Code p. 93).
SR5.SpriteMajorPower_coRoutine_D: The compiler picks a target: the sprite's level is added to the dice pool of its next matrix test, or taken from it (Kill Code p. 92).
SR5.SpriteMachineDescription:
Of all the sprites, the Machine sprite is the most likely to interact with the physical world, although that would happen through a device. They’re experts at all sorts of electronics.

The electronics sprite: affects the physical world through devices.

SR5 p. 259
SR5.STATUSES_Antenna_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: no more communications or wireless.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.STATUSES_Axle_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: Speed drops to 1.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.STATUSES_BleedOut_GE:
Target suffers 1P DV, unresisted, for every Action they perform that is not First Aid until a successful Logic + First Aid [Mental] (4) Test is made) or a Heal spell is cast on them and removes at least 1 box of damage).

Every action other than First Aid costs 1 box of Physical damage, unresisted, until a First Aid + Logic [Mental] (4) Test succeeds or a Heal spell removes at least 1 box.

Run & Gun p. 114
SR5.STATUSES_Blinded_GE:
One eye: –4 all actions involving sight; Two eyes: –8 on all actions, no vision-based Perception tests allowed for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.

One eye: −4 dice on actions that need sight. Both eyes: −8 dice on everything and no visual Perception Tests. Lasts as many Combat Turns as the original DV.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_BrokenGrip_GE:
Target is unable to maintain their grip on anything in their hand, suffers a –1 dice pool penalty per injured arm for all Subduing or Clinching attacks, and drops any item in their hand for a number of Combat Turns equal to the DV of the attack.

Cannot hold anything and drops what is in hand, for as many Combat Turns as the original DV; −1 die per injured arm on Subduing or Clinching attacks.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_Buckled_GE:
Target makes Body (DV) Test or else they hit the ground and stay there for (DV)-hits Combat Turns.

Body (DV) Test; on a failure, down on the ground for (DV − hits) Combat Turns.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_Deafened_GE:
One ear: –2 all actions involving hearing; Two ears: –4 on all actions, no hearing-based Perception tests allowed for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.

One ear: −2 dice on actions that need hearing. Both ears: −4 dice on everything and no hearing Perception Tests. Lasts as many Combat Turns as the original DV.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_DirtyTrick_GE:
This shot does no damage, but the opponent receives a -{value} penalty on next action. Pulling a Dirty Trick shot with different types of ammo can enhance the effect.

No damage. With at least 1 net hit, the opponent's next action takes a -{value} dice pool modifier (distraction); some ammo types make it worse.

SR5 p. 195
SR5.STATUSES_DoorLock_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: that door stays shut.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.STATUSES_EngineBlock_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: the vehicle is disabled.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.NetEntangled_GE:
Subdued: no action that needs physical movement, counts as prone for any attack against them. To get free: Complex action, Unarmed Combat + Agility or Escape Artist + Agility, threshold {threshold}.

Caught in the net: the target is subdued (SR5 p. 195), can take no action that requires moving, and counts as prone against any attack. To break out: Complex Action, Agility + Unarmed Combat or Agility + Escape Artist, threshold {threshold}.

Run & Gun p. 25

SR5.NetAlreadyCaught: {name} is already caught in a net.
SR5.NetEscapeButton: Get free from the net (threshold {threshold}, Complex action)
SR5.NetSizeXL: XL net on a normal-size target (Agility −2)
SR5.NetSizeLarge: Standard net on a large target (Agility +2)
SR5.NetShockCharge_GE:
The second electric charge goes off at the start of the next Combat Turn.

Two discharges for the ShockNet: one on impact, the other when the next Combat Turn begins.

Run & Gun p. 28
SR5.STATUSES_Entanglement_GE:
The character can use a rope or whip-like weapon to entangle her opponents instead of outright killing them. In an Armed Combat Attack using an Exotic Melee Weapon Skill, the character can use net hits from the attack to reduce the opponent’s Agility for that Action Phase instead of dealing damage from the weapon. If the attack generated any net hits at all, the opponent cannot move any further away from the character than the range of the weapon. If the opponent’s Agility is reduced to 0, the opponent can do no other action than attempt to break free. Like a subdual or clinch, the opponent will have to break free of the entanglement in order restore his agility attribute. If they want to get away, the opponent can attempt an Escape Artist + Agility [Physical] Test as a Complex Action with a threshold of the number of successes used to reduce his Agility. If successful, the opponent is free and no longer suffers from the Agility penalty. Weapons that can be used with this called shot include: chain whip, leather whip, manrike, kusarigama, rope dart, and lariat. Note that use of this action requires Martial Art training

Melee attack with a whip (not monofilament), chain, rope, lariat…; requires martial arts training. No damage: the target's Agility drops by the net hits, and with at least 1 net hit they cannot move farther away than the weapon's reach. At Agility 0 they can only try to break free: Complex Action, Escape Artist + Agility [Physical], threshold = net hits.

Run & Gun p. 111
SR5.STATUSES_Fatigued_GE:
Target makes a secondary Damage Resistance Test using Body only against Stun damage equal to half the DV of the original attack.

Second resistance test, Body alone, against Stun damage equal to half the original DV.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.STATUSES_Feint_GE:
Close combat only. Fake attack with no damage: on the real attack, in the next Action Phase, the opponent's defense loses as many dice as the feint's net hits. Feints do not add up: only the last one counts.

Run & Gun p. 111
SR5.STATUSES_Flared_GE:
–8 penalty on any action taken in the character’s next Action Phase, no vision-based Perception tests allowed for thirty seconds (ten Combat Rounds).

Flare round in the face: −8 dice on every action in the next Action Phase, and no visual Perception Tests for 10 Combat Turns (30 seconds).

Run & Gun p. 116
SR5.STATUSES_FuelTankBattery_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: the vehicle is disabled and leaks fuel or charge.

Run & Gun p. 115
SR5.STATUSES_Knockdown_GE:
Target must make a Strength + Agility (DV+3) Test or fall prone.

Strength + Agility (DV + 3) Test or fall prone; the target can get up as soon as their next Action Phase.

Run & Gun p. 114
SR5.STATUSES_Nauseous_GE:
Target makes a Body + Willpower (4) roll; each hit less than the required 4 causes the target to double over and begin vomiting for one Combat Turn. Vomiting targets suffer a –4 dice pool penalty to all actions.

Body + Willpower (4) Test: each missing hit means 1 Combat Turn spent vomiting, at −4 dice on every action.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_OneArmBandit_GE:
Target’s arm is ineffective and they are unable to perform any actions with that limb for a number of Combat Turns equal to the DV of the attack; they also suffer a –6 dice pool penalty until that arm is healed), Weak Side (target suffers a –2 dice penalty on all melee Defense tests while their arm is ineffective/

Arm out of action for as many Combat Turns as the original DV, then −6 dice on actions using it until it is healed.

Run & Gun p. 114
SR5.STATUSES_OnPinsAndNeedles_GE:
Rough Terrain (Requires 1 shot per square meter, 1/2 Movement through terrain; if the target is barefoot they suffer 3P resisted with Body)

Flechettes scattered on the ground: difficult terrain (1 shot per square meter). Barefoot, the target moves at half speed and takes 3P, resisted with Body.

Run & Gun p. 117
SR5.STATUSES_Pin_GE:
With an appropriate ranged weapon, the character can pin an opponent to the floor, the ground, or a wall. On a successful attack with the weapon, if the DV exceeds the Armor Rating of the target’s clothing (meaning augmentations like dermal plating would not be taken into account), then the flesh and clothing of the opponent are pinned to that object. Net hits determine how securely the opponent is pinned. While the opponent is pinned, he suffers a –2 penalty to all Defense Tests. To break free of a pin, the character can make a Body + Strength [Physical] Test as a Simple Action with a threshold of the net hits of the pin. The character can also rip himself free as a Free Action, but takes 1 box of unresisted physical damage for each net hit on the Pin Called Shot. Both the Simple and Free Action can be attempted in the same Action Phase. If the Simple Action fails, the difference between the hits rolled and the threshold are added to the Physical Damage the character takes when attempting to break free. Note that use of this action requires Martial Art training.

Bow or throwing weapon; requires martial arts training. If the DV beats the Armor of the clothing alone, the target is pinned: −2 dice on defense. Breaking free: Simple Action, Strength + Body [Physical], threshold = net hits; or tearing loose as a Free Action for 1 unresisted Physical box per net hit. If the Simple Action fails, the shortfall adds to the tearing damage.

Run & Gun p. 112
SR5.INFO_BlightDrops: Blight on {actor}: cut from the manasphere, end of {list}. Nothing comes back by itself when the effect ends: foci are switched on again by hand.
SR5.STATUSES_Shaked_GE:
Intimidating shot: Composure (2) Test, or −1 die (target shaken).

Run & Gun p. 117

Physical Damage attacks only, must be with piercing weapon; injuries cause the target to bleed internally, suffering unresisted 2S DV every minute until a Medicine + Logic [Mental] (16, 1 minute) Extended Test, First Aid + Logic [Mental] (16, 1 minute) Extended Test is successful, or a Heal spell is cast on them and removes at least 1 box of damage.

Piercing weapon and Physical damage only: 2S unresisted every minute, until an Extended Test (16, 1 minute) of Logic + Medicine or Logic + First Aid [Mental] succeeds, or a Heal spell removes at least 1 box.

SR5.STATUSES_Slowed_GE:
Target’s Movement, both Walk and Run rate, is halved and no Sprint Tests are allowed.

Walk and run rates halved; no sprinting.

SR5.STATUSES_Stunned_GE:
Body + Willpower Test to resist or target receives a penalty to Initiative Score. Threshold and penaly depend on location.

Body + Willpower Test, or the Initiative Score drops; threshold and drop depend on the location hit.

SR5.STATUSES_TrickShot_GE:
Net hits on this Called Shot add to the shooter’s dice pool on Intimidation Tests against the target.

Prepared show-off shot, outside the heat of combat: −4 dice on top of the usual modifiers, no damage. Its hits add as dice to the next Intimidation Test against the target by the shooter or a known ally.

SR5 p. 196
SR5.STATUSES_UnableToSpeak_GE:
The target loses the ability to form understandable speech. They can mutter, gesture, groan, and drool, but everything they try to speak comes out as gibberish. This lasts for 1 hour x DV of the shot.

Speech comes out as gibberish (grunts and gestures only) for 1 hour per point of DV.

Run & Gun p. 114
SR5.STATUSES_WeakSide_GE:
The target suffers a –1 dice pool penalty on all melee Defense tests while they suffer from the effects of Broken Grip.

−1 die on all melee defenses while Broken Grip or One-arm Bandit lasts.

Run & Gun p. 113
SR5.STATUSES_Winded_GE:
Target is unable to perform Complex Actions for a number of Combat Turns equal to the original DV of the attack.

No Complex Actions for as many Combat Turns as the original DV.

SR5.STATUSES_WindowMotor_GE:
Vehicle called shot, effect applied only if the vehicle takes damage after its resistance test: the power window is stuck.

SR5.WARN_StorageNoVehicleToStore: No vehicle or drone to park: they are all parked, or this character owns none.
SR5.JammerHint: SR5 p. 441: Noise equal to the Device Rating (else the item's rating), reduced by 1 every 5 m (area) or 20 m (30-degree cone). The wearer suffers it too. Walls are left to the gamemaster.
SR5.JammerSparedHint: Only applies while the item's wireless mode is on.
SR5.GearIsIntangibleHint: A contract, a licence, a subscription… owned, but not a thing you can put away.
SR5.NotSizeAdaptedHint: SR5 p. 420: an item not made for its holder’s size (human-sized in a dwarf’s or a troll’s hands, or the reverse) costs −2 dice on its tests. A troll with Delicate Fingers (The Complete Trog p. 188) has no such penalty. Unticked, the item is fitted: the lifestyle paid for it.
SR5.StorageGarageHint: A garage holds a single vehicle (Run Faster p. 221). Buy several garages to hold several.
