A garage is a lifestyle Asset with a minimum lifestyle per vehicle (Run Faster p. 221). Uncheck if your table does not track lifestyles.
SR5.HELP_StorageDropMsg: The storage appears at the character's feet with everything in it. The gear leaves the sheet and goes with it.
SR5.HELP_StoragePickUpMsg: The storage and what is in it come back to the character's sheet.
SR5.StorageLockedHidden: This container is locked: its contents stay hidden until it is open.
SR5.StorageLockTest: Locksmith + Agility [Physical], extended test, 1 Combat Turn per roll (SR5 p. 359)
SR5.StorageLockNoKit: Picking a lock takes a lockpick set (SR5 p. 447).
SR5.StorageLockAntiTamperHeld: Anti-tamper system of {storage} defeated by {actor} ({hits} / {threshold} hits).
SR5.StorageLockGlitchNote: Glitch: the GM may take 1D6 hits away from the total (SR5 p. 48).
SR5.StorageLockNoPool: Without the Locksmith skill, no lockpicking: it cannot be defaulted.
SR5.StorageLockOwnershipHint: Locked storage: the rights shown are the ones you mean to give. Above Limited, they only apply once it is open; until then, everyone stays at Limited at most.
SR5.StorageLockAlarm: Alarm: the anti-tamper system of {storage} went off while {actor} was picking it ({hits} / {threshold} hits).
SR5.StorageLockHackCard: {actor} wants to hack the wireless maglock of {storage} (rating {rating}): Control Device, 2 marks, Electronic Warfare + Intuition [Sleaze] vs Intuition + Firewall (SR5 p. 238-239). The GM opens the lock if the action succeeds.
SR5.WARN_StorageLockTooFar: The character must stand beside the container, on the same scene.
SR5.SETTINGS_LockpickRequiresKit_D: Book rule (SR5 p. 447): without a lockpick set or an autopicker in the inventory, no lockpicking. Untick to do without.
SR5.HELP_StorageLootMsg: The gear goes to the character whose token is selected on the scene — not necessarily the one who put the storage down.
SR5.SETTINGS_StarterKit_D: Each player character created in the world (not one taken from a compendium) gets a "Backpack" storage, a "Locker" storage and an empty standard credstick (5,000¥ at most). Only what it lacks; the characters already in the world get nothing.
SR5.SETTINGS_StorageDropOnDeath_D: When a character dies, a bag appears on the body with part of what they carried. Table comfort: no SR5 rule asks for this.
SR5.SETTINGS_StorageDropOnDeathShare_D: Each carried item has this percent chance of ending up in the spoils. 50 by default.
SR5.SETTINGS_SubActorFolder_T: Folder of the actors made from a sheet
SR5.SETTINGS_SubActorFolder_D: Where the spirits, drones, vehicles, sprites, agents, contacts and bags a sheet brings out are put. "Sheet's folder": the same folder as the sheet; a sheet at the root or from a compendium sends them to "Temporary actors". That folder is made once by the GM, then reused, even renamed.
SR5.SETTINGS_WifiRequiresDNI_T: Require a DNI to switch the wireless as a free action
SR5.SETTINGS_BlockMissingActions_T: Block an action the character no longer has
SR5.SETTINGS_BlockMissingActions_D: Per initiative pass, a character has one free action, and two simple actions or one complex action (SR5 p. 162-163). When checked, an action no longer available in combat is refused with a warning, and nothing is spent. When unchecked (default), it still goes through, as before.
SR5.SETTINGS_GMOnlyItemEffects_T: Item effects written by the gamemaster only
SR5.SETTINGS_GMOnlyItemEffects_D: When checked, only the gamemaster adds, changes or removes the effects of an item (tab Modifiers): a player sees them but cannot edit them, so that nobody grants themselves a bonus. When unchecked (default), the owner of an item edits its effects, as before.
SR5.SETTINGS_CheckPlayerRolls_D: When checked, the gamemaster counts the hits of a player's card again on its dice, within the pool of the sheet (Edge included), and is warned of any gap. When unchecked (default), a card rolled for an actor its author owns stands as written, as a gamemaster's. Either way, a card for an actor its author does not own is refused, and the gamemaster keeps the window "A player asks the GM" when a card touches what another owns. When unchecked, three confirmations of the hits of a player's card no longer open: the effect that reads the hits, the attack of an IC and the toxin card.
SR5.SETTINGS_WifiRequiresDNI_D: Switching a device is a free action through a direct neural interface (SR5 p. 163), a simple action otherwise (p. 164). When checked, each character's "Wired by DNI" box decides. When unchecked (default), switching the wireless is a free action for everyone. Same rule for a firearm with its wireless on: ejecting the clip and changing the firing mode are free with a DNI (p. 424 and 432); the choke too, by ruling (by analogy with p. 163).
SR5.HELP_DNIWiredMsg: The character commands their devices through a direct neural interface: switching their wireless is a free action (SR5 p. 163), a simple action otherwise (p. 164). With a firearm whose wireless is on, ejecting the clip and changing the firing mode are free too (p. 424 and 432), and the choke by ruling (by analogy with p. 163). Only counts when the world setting asks for it.

SR5.SETTINGS_PickpocketThiefChooses_D: House rule. By default the GM chooses the object lifted (SR5 p. 419). Ticked, the thief chooses it himself before his roll, with no GM validation.

SR5.SETTINGS_ConvergenceThreshold_D: Overwatch Score at which the grid converges: 40 by the book (SR5 p. 232, Kill Code p. 29); another value is a house rule. The Wanted by GOD quality lowers it by 10 (30 by the book, Data Trails p. 49). When it is crossed, the gamemaster gets an 'Apply the convergence' card (unless the Matrice module is active, which tells it itself).
SR5.SETTINGS_OverwatchGMOnly_T: Overwatch Score kept by the gamemaster
SR5.SETTINGS_OverwatchGMOnly_D: Checked (book rule, SR5 p. 231): when the Overwatch Score rises, only the gamemaster sees the number; the player learns it with the Check Overwatch Score action or the Baby Monitor program. Unchecked: the number also shows to whoever acted. The sheet always shows it to the gamemaster, or to whoever runs Baby Monitor.
SR5.SETTINGS_HostNodes_D: Off the book (Core p. 233 slaves no host). Checked: on a host's sheet, "PAN master" offers the other hosts; the slaved host hangs in its master's crown and defends with it when the master is the stronger, as a device of its WAN. Unchecked (default): the book's rule.
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownVisibility_D: Book rules (SR5 p. 235-237): everyone sees their own crown, and of the others the devices they spotted (wireless on within 100 m of their antenna, those they marked or spotted with Matrix Perception). The gamemaster decides: a player only sees their own crown and the devices the gamemaster revealed by clicking the icon. The gamemaster sees everything, and a yellow ring shows what the players do not see.
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownRevealScope_D: To the whole table (default): a device the gamemaster reveals from its icon's menu is seen by every player. Player by player: the gamemaster ticks the characters it is revealed to; the others only see it by the visibility rules.
SR5.PanCrownRevealToIntro: Tick the characters {name} is revealed to:
SR5.PanCrownRevealToNone: No player character on this scene.
SR5.SETTINGS_RuleLocksGMExempt_T: The gamemaster is never stopped by rule locks
SR5.SETTINGS_RuleLocksGMExempt_D: Checked: when the gamemaster acts himself (NPCs, or a character he plays), a rule lock does not stop him; the action goes and a notification tells him which rule he passed. Unchecked (default): the gamemaster is refused like anyone. Players always follow the boxes of the rule locks menu.
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownOpening_D: For you only. The "PAN" button of a token's HUD and the AR view key are always available. On hover: a token's crown opens when the pointer passes over it. Always visible: the crowns of every visible token stay open.
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownArKey_D: For you only. Toggle: one press shows the crowns of every visible token, a second hides them. Hold: they stay shown while the key is down. The key is set in "Configure Controls" (M by default).
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownAmbience_D: For you only, as your machine allows. Static: the crown without animation. Sober: it unfolds from the token and pulses run along the lines. Spectacular: also a halo, a flicker of the icons and a rain of code on the crowns opened one by one. The gamemaster sets a ceiling; if your system asks for reduced motion, or if Foundry's performance mode is "Low", the crown stays static.
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownAmbienceCap_T: Ambience ceiling of the PAN crowns
SR5.SETTINGS_PanCrownAmbienceCap_D: The richest ambience allowed at the table. Each player chooses their own in their settings, up to this ceiling.
SR5.KEYBINDING_PanCrownArView_D: Shows the PAN crowns of every visible token, as a toggle or while held, per the "AR view key" setting.

SR5.ToxinEffectAgony_GE:
The character is broken by an unbearable pain that is difficult to describe. If the residual Power of the toxin exceeds the character's Willpower, he or she can no longer speak coherently or move faster than by crawling slowly.

Overwhelming pain: if the remaining Power exceeds Willpower, the victim cannot speak coherently and can only crawl.

Bullets & Bandages p. 20
SR5.ToxinEffectArcaneInhibitor_GE:
Venom with this quality temporarily reduces the victim’s Magic by the Power of the venom. If the Power is greater than the victim’s Magic Rating, they cannot use Magic until the power of the venom is reduced. As the Power is reduced, Magic comes back normally.

Venom: the victim's Magic drops by the venom's Power; if Power exceeds Magic, no magic at all. Magic returns as the Power wears down.

Howling Shadows p. 194
SR5.ToxinEffectDisorientation_GE:
Disorientation causes the victim a –2 dice pool modifier to all actions for ten minutes, due to confusion and disorientation.

−2 dice on every action for 10 minutes.

SR5 p. 409
SR5.ToxinEffectNausea_GE:
Nausea is a catch-all term; it includes pain, panic, vomiting, and double vision. If the Power of an attack after the Toxin Resistance Test exceeds the target’s Willpower, he is incapacitated (unable to take any actions) with vomiting and dizziness for 3 Combat Turns. Whether or not a character is incapacitated, Nausea doubles all of a character’s wound modifiers for ten minutes. A nauseated character with 3 boxes of damage (a –1 wound modifier), for example, suffers –2 dice on all tests instead.

If Power after resistance exceeds Willpower: unable to act for 3 Combat Turns (vomiting, dizziness). Either way, wound modifiers are doubled for 10 minutes.

SR5 p. 409
SR5.ToxinEffectParalysis_GE:
Paralysis renders the victim unable to move by blocking the body’s neuromuscular signals. If the Power of an attack after the Toxin Resistance Test exceeds the target’s Reaction, the target is paralyzed and unable to take physical actions for 1 hour. Even if the target is not paralyzed, he suffers a –2 dice pool modifier for the next hour.

If Power after resistance exceeds Reaction: no physical actions for 1 hour. Otherwise, −2 dice for that hour.

SR5 p. 409

SR5.WARN_NoTemplateForBlast: This throw's template was removed: the distance to the blast cannot be measured. Place it again or settle the damage by hand.
SR5.WARN_ScatterCardTooOld: This card predates template tracking: it cannot tell which template is its own. Roll the scatter by hand and move the template yourself.
SR5.WARN_TemplateNotYours: This template was placed by someone else: only its author or the GM can move or remove it.
SR5.WARN_NotEnoughAction: Not enough actions left ! You need at least {value} {action} action.
SR5.WARN_OnlyOneTradition: You can have only one tradition.
SR5.WARN_RemoveClipFirst: You must first remove clip / belt / drum.
SR5.WARN_SpellShapingMaxMagic: You may not take more dice worth of penalty than your Magic Rating ({magic}).
SR5.INFO_SparedBySpellShaping: {name} stands in a Spell Shaping bubble: the spell leaves them untouched.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpellShapingBubbleCost_D: Spell Shaping (SR5 p. 326): how many shaping points spare one character. A bubble is 1 metre in radius, which cannot be modelled on a battle grid, so the system approximates it as "one point spares one character". This is an approximation: the book gives no conversion.
SR5.SETTINGS_SpellShapingBubbleCost_T: Spell Shaping: cost of one bubble
SR5.SpellShapingSpare: Spare the targeted or selected tokens
SR5.WARN_SpellShapingNoBubbleLeft: Every declared bubble is already used ({number}).
SR5.WARN_SpellShapingNoTokenSelected: Target (T key) or select the tokens to spare on the scene first.
SR5.SpellShapingPickHint: Tick the characters to spare (bubbles left: {number}).
SR5.WARN_EmulateMaxDepth: The emulated rating cannot exceed Depth ({depth}).
SR5.WARN_TargetWirelessOff: This drone has its wireless off: no wireless Matrix action reaches it (SR5 p. 421). Only a direct connection can (p. 233): to play one, switch its wireless on for the action.
SR5.WARN_BlightNoSpell: Cut from the manasphere by Blight: no magic until the effect ends, no spell, ritual, conjuring, counterspelling, alchemy, astral (perception, projection, Assensing and Astral Combat), focus or sustained spell; adept powers are off (Better Than Bad p. 157). A preparation already made can still be triggered.
SR5.INFO_PreparationSpent: {actor}: the preparation {item} has lost all its Potency, its magic is gone (SR5 p. 305).
SR5.WARN_PreparationDecayGMOnly: The start and the pace of a preparation's loss of Potency are set by the gamemaster.
SR5.WARN_PreparationRestored: {user} changed the start or pace of a preparation ({name}, {actor}), reserved to the GM: the GM's value is put back.
SR5.WARN_PreparationSpent: This preparation has no Potency left: its magic is gone, the spell is lost (SR5 p. 305).
SR5.WARN_TargetTooMany: You must choose only one target (token)
SR5.WARN_FanningTooMany: Flamethrower fanning: three targets at most.
SR5.WARN_FanningOutOfRange: Flamethrower fanning: every target must be within the weapon's range.
SR5.WARN_FanningTooFar: Flamethrower fanning: each target must be within 4 m of another.
SR5.WARN_FiringModeAmmo: This firing mode needs {needed} units of ammo, {left} left.
SR5.WARN_SuppressiveFireEmpty: Suppressive fire: the magazine is empty (at least one round is needed; under 20, the zone narrows, SR5 p. 180).
SR5.INFO_SuppressiveFireNarrowed: Suppressive fire with {left} rounds: the suppression zone is only {width} m wide (1 m less for every 2 missing rounds, SR5 p. 179).
SR5.WARN_TargetTroughAndInto: You must choose the first of the two targets (token).
SR5.WeaponAccessorySlotBarrel: Replacing or adding to the barrel
SR5.WeaponAccessorySlotSide: On the side of the weapon
SR5.WeaponAccessorySlotStock: Replacing or adding to the stock
SR5.WeaponAccessorySpecialEffect_D: The rule the system applies for this accessory: a homemade flashlight lights like a flashlight, a smartgun system gives its dice, etc.
SR5.WeaponAccessoryPriceMultiplier_D: For an accessory whose price depends on the weapon carrying it: its price is this multiple of the weapon's base price (long barrel: 1, Hard Targets p. 183; ceramic / plasteel components: the rating, p. 180; internal smartgun: 1, SR5 p. 432). At 0, the accessory has its own price. Otherwise the shop sells it on the weapon's Armory.
SR5.WirelessHeldByDeployedDrone: Wireless handled by the deployed drone
SR5.SituationalTargetMetatypeHint: The box ticks itself when the targeted character matches. With no target, or a target with no metatype, it stays to be ticked by hand (The Complete Trog p. 188).
SR5.AddictionWorsen: Failed: the addiction worsens by one level
SR5.AddictionAlreadyWorsened: {drug}: the addiction already gained its level for this test. An addiction both physiological and psychological is tested with both pools, but only one level is gained even if both tests fail (SR5 p. 414).
SR5.AddictionBurnoutEither: Body or Willpower, by a coin toss (tie, SR5 p. 414)
SR5.AddictionBurnoutLoss: {name} fails an addiction test ({drug}) at Burnout: 1 point of {attribute} is lost for good, and 1 point of its maximum (SR5 p. 414). At 0, coma: both monitors filled, plus 1 box of physical overflow. To apply by hand.
SR5.AddictionTestReminder: {drug}: an addiction test will be due after {weeks} weeks of use (11 − rating {rating}), threshold {threshold}. Roll it from the Addictions list, Qualities tab (SR5 p. 414).
SR5.WARN_AddictionNotFound: This addiction is no longer on the sheet.
SR5.HELP_AddictionTestMsg: Body + Willpower when physiological, Logic + Willpower when psychological, both tests when both: one failure is enough (SR5 p. 414). The threshold is the Addiction Threshold.
SR5.HELP_AddictionLevelMsg: The Addiction quality (SR5 p. 77-78): Mild, Moderate, Severe, Burnout. Each failed test raises it one level.
SR5.MilkBrickUsed: {name}: the brick of milk removes {removed} (No Future p. 172).
SR5.MilkBrickNothing: {name}: the brick of milk is drunk but removes nothing: no Nausea or Disorientation it soothes (No Future p. 172).
SR5.WARN_MilkBrickNotOwner: You do not own {name}: the brick of milk is not used. Ask the gamemaster.
SR5.AddictionResistanceNote: Applies to every addiction test. Drug Tolerant (Chrome Flesh p. 54) only covers natural and synthetic drugs.
SR5.FACTION_OnlyGM: Only the active gamemaster edits factions.
SR5.FACTION_MenuHint: Faction Reputation (Cutting Aces p. 156): factions, members, movements, spending and journal. Gamemaster only.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_MenuHint: Actors and contacts imported before the Negotiation fix lost it (0). The window lists those whose source compendium gives more, and the gamemaster ticks what applies; each correction is applied once per sheet.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_Intro: These sheets read a Negotiation of 0 while their source compendium gives one. A 0 set on purpose looks the same as a lost one: tick only what you want back. A sheet already restored is not offered again; what is left unticked stays.
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_All: Repair all (ticks every sheet at 0 in the list)
SR5.NEGO_REPAIR_OnlyActiveGM: Only the active gamemaster can apply the repair.
SR5.FACTION_Hint: Faction Reputation (Cutting Aces p. 156-160). Pending movements apply at the end of the mission, with Karma. The gamemaster always keeps the last word on NPC attitude.
SR5.FACTION_DeleteConfirm: Delete the faction {name} and its whole journal?
SR5.FACTION_Pending: Pending (applied at the end of the mission)
SR5.FACTION_ApplyPending: End of mission: apply pending movements
SR5.FACTION_DropActor: Drop an NPC or a vendor here from the actors sidebar to affiliate it with this faction (it leaves any other faction).
SR5.FACTION_DropNoPc: A player character is not a faction member: their standing is kept in the journal.
SR5.FACTION_DropNoPack: An actor from a compendium cannot join a faction: import it into the world first, then drop it from the Actors sidebar.
SR5.FACTION_PickFactionActor: Choose a faction and at least one character.
SR5.FACTION_NotEnough: Not enough reputation: {score} for a cost of {cost} (never below zero, p. 159).
SR5.FACTION_ContactNotInFaction: This contact must belong to this character and to this faction.
SR5.FACTION_OnceAMonth: This contact's Influence was already raised this month (once a month, p. 159). Go on anyway?
SR5.FAVOR_BalanceHint: One chip per Favor Rating (Run Faster p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_PillContactOwes: Favor chips: the contact owes you
SR5.FAVOR_PillCharacterOwes: Favor chips: you owe the contact
SR5.FAVOR_RelationHint: Family: a favor costs one chip less, Loyalty −1 in dice. Blackmail: favors cost nothing, the relationship never improves (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_IntimidatedHint: The character intimidated this contact: the relationship can no longer improve (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_Source: Favors: core rulebook; chips: Run Faster p. 176 sq..
SR5.FAVOR_AskHint: Rating ≤ Loyalty: the contact agrees. Above: opposed Negotiation + Charisma [Social] test, with the Loyalty and the chips spent as dice (core rulebook, RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_AskRule: The contact grants a favor whose rating does not exceed their Loyalty ({loyalty}). Above it they must be convinced with an opposed Negotiation + Charisma [Social] test; their Loyalty adds to your pool, and each chip spent adds one die, +4 at most.
SR5.FAVOR_SpendChips: Chips spent (+1 die each, {max} at most)
SR5.FAVOR_GrantedWithin: Favor rating {rating} ≤ Loyalty {loyalty}: the contact agrees (core rulebook).
SR5.FAVOR_TestNeeded: Favor rating {rating} > Loyalty {loyalty}: opposed Negotiation + Charisma [Social] test. The Loyalty and chip dice wait in the roll dialog. If the gamemaster says the favor is granted, click "Favor obtained".
SR5.FAVOR_NoActor: This contact belongs to no character: no test to roll.
SR5.FAVOR_ObtainedHint: The contact gains chips equal to the favor's rating, minus the chips you still held on them (RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_ObtainedRule: The contact gains chips equal to the Rating of the favor, minus any remaining chips the character has with them (RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_ServiceHint: A service done for the contact, asked or not: a chip for the character (RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_ServiceRule: Good work done for the contact, or a favor they asked of you and you completed: "this is considered a chip" (RF p. 176). The gamemaster may count more.
SR5.FAVOR_RepayHint: The contact demands twice the value: two favors of the same rating, one of double rating, or about twice the market value (RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_RepayRule: You owe {debt} chip(s). The contact generally demands twice the value: favors given back for a total rating of {double}, or a payment of about twice the market value of the original favor (RF p. 176). Time for a nuyen debt: 4 weeks up to 100 ¥, 3 up to 1,000 ¥, 2 up to 10,000 ¥, 1 beyond; then a Loyalty test each week (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_RepayNothing: This clears no chip: twice the value must be given back.
SR5.FAVOR_ImproveHint: Spend chips and weeks equal to the Loyalty aimed at (RF p. 176).
SR5.FAVOR_ImproveRule: Going to Loyalty {target} costs {cost} chip(s) and {weeks} week(s) of interaction with the contact (RF p. 176). The gamemaster may make some of it part of an adventure.
SR5.FAVOR_ImproveRefused_chips: You need {cost} chip(s) on the contact to reach Loyalty {target}.
SR5.FAVOR_ImproveRefused_intimidated: This contact was intimidated: the relationship can no longer improve (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_ImproveRefused_blackmail: A blackmailed contact does not improve: their Loyalty measures your leverage (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_IntimidateHint: Get a favor through intimidation: no chip, but −1 Loyalty and no improvement ever again (Run Faster).
SR5.FAVOR_IntimidateRule: Intimidation gets the favor without paying or owing chips, but costs 1 Loyalty at once and forever removes the chance to improve the relationship (Run Faster). Roll the Intimidation test separately.
SR5.FAVOR_IntimidateBlackmail: Blackmailed contact: intimidation costs no Loyalty (Run Faster). Roll the Intimidation test separately.
SR5.FAVOR_AdjustHint: Add or remove chips by hand, with a reason.
SR5.FAVOR_AdjustValue: Chips (+ the contact owes, − you owe)
SR5.FAVOR_NotOwner: Only the gamemaster and the character's owner keep these chips.
SR5.FAVOR_LogSpent: {n} chip(s) spent on a rating {rating} favor
SR5.FAVOR_LogRepaidFavors: Repaid with favors of total rating {value}: {n} chip(s)
SR5.INFOBROKER_Tagline: Knowledge comes at a price (Cutting Aces, Information for Sale).
SR5.INFOBROKER_BuyRule: Choose the kind of data and on whom. The gamemaster sets the price within the book's range and says whether the data can be found; the gamemaster has the final say on its availability.
SR5.INFOBROKER_SellRule: Offer the broker a file from your inventory. No book prices what a broker pays: the gamemaster bids, you accept or not. You keep your copy.
SR5.INFOBROKER_PickType: Choose a kind of data first.
SR5.INFOBROKER_NoBuyer: No character of yours to buy or sell.
SR5.INFOBROKER_OutOfRange: Outside the book's range (allowed, gamemaster's call).
SR5.INFOBROKER_NotActiveGM: Only the active gamemaster keeps the broker's register.
SR5.INFOBROKER_CardPaid: {actor} pays {price} for "{name}". The file comes when the broker has it.
SR5.INFOBROKER_Source: Information for sale: Cutting Aces; the broker as a contact: Hard Targets; false information: core rulebook, contact complications.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_accessCodes: Admin codes, digital keys, back doors; they change fast.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_address: From mailing lists to safehouses, haunts and associates.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_blackmail: Leverage: valuable, risky, often real legwork.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_handwriting: To forge a signature, or read a character.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_history: A life's trail; the more detail, the more it costs.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_marketScan: Every seller of an item: lowers its Availability for that purchase (the gamemaster says by how much).
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_medical: Strengths, weaknesses, allergies; often well guarded.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_name: A name for a face, SINs and aliases.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_patterns: A target's habits, to predict their moves.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_psychProfile: A psychological portrait, found or built.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_purchases: Credit history; cash goes by word of mouth.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_safehouses: Places likely in use, from utilities and traffic.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_socialMedia: The whole online presence: opinions, tastes, way of talking.
SR5.INFOBROKER_TypeHint_workplace: Employer and position; dearer for freelancers or the SINless.
SR5.SOCIALTRAIT_IgnoreNegative: Good Looking: negative modifiers ignored (Cutting Aces)
SR5.SOCIALTRAIT_Effect_socialIgnoreNegat: Ignore 2 points of negative Social modifiers (Good Looking and Knows It, Cutting Aces)
SR5.SOCIALTRAIT_Effect_etiquetteIntuitio: Intuition for Charisma on Etiquette (Empathic Listener, Cutting Aces)
SR5.SOCIALTRAIT_Effect_influenceLogic: Logic for Charisma on Intimidation, Leadership, Negotiation (Master Debater, Cutting Aces)
SR5.SETTINGS_CuttingAcesSocial_D: Offers the social maneuvers (Cutting Aces p. 153-154) and the steps of a con under way (p. 162-164) in the roll dialog. Nothing applies unless chosen. Unticked, the social tests stay those of the core rulebook; the con tracker stays open to the GM.
SR5.CON_MenuHint: The cons under way, their Intel Level and Prop Rating, step by step (Cutting Aces p. 162-164).
SR5.CON_OnlyGM: Only the active GM keeps the con tracker.
SR5.CON_NeedArtist: Tick at least one con artist.
SR5.CON_DeleteConfirm: Delete the con "{name}" and its log?
SR5.CON_EvaluationLocked: Evaluating the target needs an Intel Level of 1 or more (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_NeedOpposition: Type the target's hits: its pool is not known.
SR5.CON_StepClosed: This step is no longer open for this con.
SR5.CON_Intel_D: Raised by investigation, matrix research, surveillance and evaluation; taken off the target's pool on the bait (Cutting Aces p. 162-163).
SR5.CON_Props_D: The sum of the props made or acquired: added to the con artist's pool on the bait (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_RolledHint: These steps are rolled from the con artist's sheet: a Con test, the step chosen in the roll dialog. Bait: +{bonus} dice for the con artist, {intel} for the target. The GM records the result from the resistance card, or by hand here.
SR5.CON_Step_investigation_D: Long con. A contact asked (SR5 p. 387): the net hits of the Negotiation test with them raise the Intel Level (Cutting Aces p. 162).
SR5.CON_Step_matrixResearch_D: Long con. A Matrix Search as an opposed test; the target's pool depends on how connected it is (Cutting Aces p. 162-163).
SR5.CON_Step_surveillance_D: Perception + Intuition against Perception + Intuition: the net hits raise or lower the Intel Level (Cutting Aces p. 162-163).
SR5.CON_Step_evaluation_D: Long con. Psychology (Profiling) + Logic [Intel Level] against the Intel Level; impossible at 0 or less (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_Step_propFabrication_D: Extended Forgery or Artisan + Agility test, threshold 2 × the rating wanted, interval 1 day; stopped short, the rating is the hits halved (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_Step_propAcquisition_D: Bought by SR5 p. 416; the GM may set Availability and cost (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_Step_bait_D: Con + Charisma + Prop Rating against the higher of Judge Intentions or Con + Intuition, less the Intel Level. Tie: wary (long con), exposed (short con) (Cutting Aces p. 163).
SR5.CON_Step_reinforce_D: Long con. Con + Charisma against Judge Intentions, without intel or props; a tie or a loss: exposed (Cutting Aces p. 164).
SR5.CON_Step_exit_D: Con + Charisma against the higher of Judge Intentions or Con + Intuition; a tie or a loss: the story crumbles, the goal is still reached (Cutting Aces p. 164).
SR5.CON_StepHint: A con under way in the GM's tracker (Cutting Aces p. 163-164): the bait adds the Prop Rating, the target resists with the higher of Judge Intentions or Con + Intuition.
SR5.CA_ManeuverHint: Cutting Aces p. 153-154: −4 dice unless stated otherwise, and one free action more.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_charmingPerformance_Effe: the NPC's attitude improves by one step (SR5 p. 140).
SR5.CA_Maneuver_drillSergeant_Effect: −2 on the target's next opposed Leadership + Willpower test against your orders.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_fauxPas_Effect: the target looks rude: −2 on its social tests next turn.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_hustle_Effect: test lost on purpose: +2 dice on the next Con or Negotiation test against the same target.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_informedOpinion_Effect: +{hits} to the Social limit for the whole encounter.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_diversion_Effect: the target takes −4 on its Perception tests until its next action.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_motivatingTeacher_Effect: +2 dice on the next Instruction test.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_peerTutoring_Effect: if every participant scores as many hits as the rank sought, the training time is reduced for all (skill between 1 and 3).
SR5.CA_Maneuver_physicalContact_Effect: +2 to Palming against that person this round.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_pushHome_Effect: the leverage bonus goes from +2 to +4 dice.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_saveFace_Effect: successful: the failed social test may be rerolled without penalty.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_drawAttention_Effect: observers get +2 to Perception against you and −2 against the others nearby (only on those who can be attracted to you).
SR5.CA_Maneuver_fakeGun_Effect: opposed by Perception + Intuition: if it works, +2 on a Con or Intimidation test against the target to make it believe you are armed.
SR5.CA_Maneuver_zanshin_Effect: opposed by the target's Judge Intentions. 1 net hit: does it have a Close Combat skill? 2: which is highest. 3: beginner (1-2), well trained (3-5) or highly trained (6+).
SR5.CA_ManeuverWaits: {name}: the outcome is read on the resistance card.
SR5.CA_ApplyNoTarget: Nothing to apply: the test had no target.
SR5.CA_PendingDrop: Drop this effect (the encounter is over)
SR5.CA_IntimidationFallout_grudge: Glitch: the target holds a grudge and plans its revenge (Cutting Aces p. 164).
SR5.CA_IntimidationFallout_enemy: Critical glitch: the target becomes a lasting enemy, out to destroy the PCs (Cutting Aces p. 164).
SR5.BARTER_NegotiationHint: Each net hit moves the offer by 10% in the characters' favour (Cutting Aces p. 161).
SR5.BARTER_IntimidationHint: Each net hit obtains 10% of the offer; without one, 250 ¥ or a true detail. No net hit: the Intimidation fails (Cutting Aces p. 164).
SR5.BARTER_TableHint: Equipment: [cost + cost × Availability × 10%] ÷ 2. Contact: Influence × 1,000 ¥. Service: (pool ÷ 4, rounded up) × 150 ¥ an hour. Information: pool × 100 ¥. The GM judges whether the NPC has what it offers (Cutting Aces p. 161-162).
SR5.IllusionNotPierced: {observer} does not see through the illusion ({spell}).
SR5.TacnetHint: At most Device Rating × 1.5 members, drones included (Run & Gun p. 105). The bearer asks, the GM confirms.
SR5.TacnetInactive: The network gives nothing until the item is active with its wireless on.
SR5.TacnetRosterHint: The roster is kept by the GM. Each member picks his combat mode skill (levels II and III).
SR5.TacnetFull: PI-Tac “{network}” is full ({max} members): {member} does not join.
SR5.TacnetRefused: The GM refuses the change of {member} in PI-Tac “{network}”.
SR5.TacnetTrimmed: The rating of “{network}” now allows {max} member(s) only: {members} leave(s) the network.
SR5.IllusionCardRejected: Illusion card ignored ({spell}, sent by {user}): it does not come from the character's owner, or its dice do not fit his pool.
SR5.IllusionConfirm: {user}: {caster} casts {spell} on {subject}. Threshold for whoever resists: {threshold}. Record it?
SR5.IllusionConfirmMismatch: The card claims {claimed} hits, its dice show {hits}: {hits} is kept.
SR5.IllusionConfirmTarget: This token was not targeted by the card's author when the roll was made.
SR5.COMMCODE_Key_D: Your character's device messaging; for the GM, the whole traffic.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_noDevice: No carried device for this messaging.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_owner: You do not speak for the holder of this device.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_noCommcode: This device has no commcode: write it on its sheet.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_offline: Your device is offline (wireless off, SR5 p. 421).
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_jammed: Your device is jammed: the jammer blocks wireless communications (SR5 p. 441).
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_bricked: Your device is bricked (Matrix monitor full, SR5 p. 228).
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_self: That is this device's own commcode.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_busy: A call is already open on one of the two devices.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_noMark: Snoop intercepts nothing without a mark on the target (SR5 p. 242).
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_gm: Only the GM speaks for a commcode with no sheet.
SR5.COMMCODE_NoCommcodeHint: This device has no commcode: write it on its sheet to send and receive.
SR5.COMMCODE_OfflineHint: Device unreachable: nothing leaves, nothing arrives. The messages sent to you wait for its return.
SR5.COMMCODE_LengthHint: Send Message (Simple Action, SR5 p. 242): one sentence, an image or a file; a paragraph through a DNI.
SR5.COMMCODE_PickThread: Pick a conversation, or type a commcode.
SR5.COMMCODE_AddTarget_D: Adds the commcode of the token you target on the map (T key).
SR5.COMMCODE_NoTarget: Target a token on the map first (T key).
SR5.COMMCODE_TargetNone: {name} has no device with a commcode.
SR5.COMMCODE_RequestSent: Request for the commcode of {name} sent to the GM.
SR5.COMMCODE_RequestActiveGM: Only the active GM answers this request.
SR5.COMMCODE_RequestAccepted: The GM gave the commcode of {target}: it is in the directory of {name}.
SR5.COMMCODE_RequestRefused: The GM refuses to give the commcode of {target}.
SR5.COMMCODE_NoContact: No contact: the commcodes your character knows are written here.
SR5.COMMCODE_InterceptHint: Snoop (SR5 p. 242): the traffic sent from or to the target, as long as your mark stays on it. To find a correspondent: Matrix Perception (SR5 p. 241); his location: Trace Icon (SR5 p. 243).
SR5.COMMCODE_GMHint: To speak for a commcode no sheet carries. For a device on a sheet, open its messaging from the sheet or the PAN crown.
SR5.COMMCODE_TraceFound: Trace Icon (SR5 p. 243): {target} is on the scene "{scene}". The location stays known while a mark of {hacker} stays on it.
SR5.COMMCODE_TraceNowhere: Trace Icon (SR5 p. 243): {target} has no token on any scene; the GM says where it is.
SR5.SETTINGS_CommcodeCipher_D: Off-book addition (the core book does not encrypt messages, SR5 p. 242). Checked: a message or file can carry a key cipher (Vigenère-like). It is set like file protection (hits = rating, SR5 p. 239); the recipient reads it with the key in their directory; an interceptor breaks it like Crack File (SR5 p. 238) and only they see the plain text. The GM always sees the plain text. Unchecked (default): nothing beyond the book.
SR5.COMMCODE_Refused_cipherOff: The commcode message cipher is not on in this world.
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherNoKey: Type a key (at least one letter).
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherSaveKey: Keep the key in the directory
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherEncrypt: Cipher the message with the key
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherHint: To cipher is to protect the message as a file (Edit File, Computer + Logic [Data Processing], p. 239). Accents drop; digits and signs stay.
SR5.COMMCODE_Cipher_wrongKey: ciphered: your key does not open it
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherCrackHint: Crack File (complex action, SR5 p. 238): Hacking + Logic [Attack] v. cipher rating x 2. The cipher's hits raise your Overwatch Score.
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherRatingHint: Cipher rating (a contact without a sheet rolls no dice)
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherProtect: {name} ciphers a message (Edit File, SR5 p. 239): {dice} dice [limit {limit}]: {faces} → rating {rating}.
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherCrackRoll: {name} cracks a ciphered message (Crack File, SR5 p. 238): {dice} dice [limit {limit}]: {faces} → {hits} hits.
SR5.COMMCODE_CipherCrack_cracked: Cipher broken: the clear text shows in your interceptions.
SR5.CIPHERTOOL_Hint: For a riddle: a text ciphered with a running key (Vigenère kind: each letter shifted by the key's letter under it, A = 0, B = 1…, the key repeated). Accents drop; digits and signs stay.
SR5.FileCipherHint: House rule (setting "Commcode message cipher"): a file ciphered with a key shows its content ciphered to whoever lacks the key, and counts as protected; a successful Crack File (SR5 p. 238) removes the cipher with the protection. The GM always reads the clear text.
SR5.FileCipher_ciphered: ciphered: without the key, the content stays unreadable
SR5.LifeStyleFirstDebit_D: The day the first month of rent is claimed (SR5 p. 370). The player chooses it while the rent has not started; the gamemaster sees it and may correct it at any time.
SR5.PRESETS_Menu_D: An automation (light or advanced) and rules (books and supplements, house rules, or both) set at once; and your own settings, saved to come back to. A preset only sets values: every setting can still be changed afterwards.
SR5.PRESETS_Intro: Choose an automation, rules, or both: the list shows what will change before you apply. Nothing is locked afterwards, each setting can still be changed in its tab.
SR5.PRESETS_Automation_light_D: Every rule lock lifted (the action goes through, the gamemaster is told), no Running status from distance, combat does not advance the clock, wireless switch free for everyone, purchases delivered at once.
SR5.PRESETS_Automation_advanced_D: Every rule lock of the book, Running status set from distance, combat advances the clock, the "Linked by DNI" box decides the wireless cost, purchases delivered after the search time.
SR5.PRESETS_Rules_book_D: Every option of the books checked (called shots, grappling, Kill Code, Rigger 5.0, Chrome Flesh, Forbidden Arcana, Bullets & Bandages…), house rules at their default. The combat options of Run & Gun (RG1 to RG6) are still picked one by one, as the book asks.
SR5.PRESETS_Rules_house_D: House rules checked (free reload, bag on the body, purchases past the creation limits…), the books' options at their default, that is the core book.
SR5.PRESETS_Rules_mixed_D: The books' options and the house rules, all checked. RG1 to RG6 are still picked one by one.
SR5.PRESETS_NoChange: This choice changes nothing: the world is already set this way.
SR5.PRESETS_RestoreConfirm: Set every world setting and the rule locks back as they were when saved?
SR5.PRESETS_File_Hint: Export the system's world settings (house rules, table options, rule locks) to a .json file, or import another gamemaster's. Compendiums, folders, registers and the state of your games do not travel.
SR5.PRESETS_File_From: Preset of the sr5 system {version}, exported on {date}.
SR5.PRESETS_File_OtherVersion: This file comes from another version of the system than yours ({version}): the settings yours does not have are ignored.
SR5.PRESETS_File_NoChange: This file changes nothing: the world is already set this way.
SR5.PRESETS_File_Ignored: Ignored (unknown to this world or not shared):
SR5.PRESETS_File_Error_format: This file is not a world preset of the sr5 system.
SR5.RULELOCKS_PresetsMoved: The "Book / Light" choice moved to the Presets (advanced / light automation), at the head of the Shadowrun settings.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGNoAttackLimit_T: RG1: no attack limit per Action Phase
SR5.SETTINGS_RGNoAttackLimit_D: Run & Gun: no more one attack per Action Phase for simple actions. The system does not count attacks per phase: the box writes the table's choice down, nothing changes in the rolls. Mind the progressive recoil, which climbs fast.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGTargetSize_D: Run & Gun: a ranged attack gains or loses dice by the target's size. Metahuman or critter by Strength + Body (2-4: −1, 5-10: 0, 11-15: +1, above: +2); drone by its category (micro −3, mini −2, small −1, medium 0, large +1); vehicle +1.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGMovementModifiers_D: Run & Gun: by the meters the target moved in its last Action Phase, a ranged attack against it loses up to 6 dice, and its own defense up to 5. The distances are those of the token in combat. Adds to the running modifiers of the core book.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGAlternativeInitiative_D: Run & Gun: the highest score acts, then loses 10 at once; the highest score left comes next, which may be the same character. The Combat Turn ends when every score is down to 0. No Initiative Passes: the pass counter stays at 1.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGArmorAsPenalty_T: RG5: aiming for the gaps in armor
SR5.SETTINGS_RGArmorAsPenalty_D: Run & Gun: the target's armor, after AP, becomes a penalty on the attack test; it no longer counts in damage resistance, and the damage keeps its type (no change to Stun). Drones and vehicles keep their armor, elemental damage its armor.
SR5.SETTINGS_RGDefenselessDamage_T: RG6: increased damage against defenseless targets
SR5.SETTINGS_RGDefenselessDamage_D: Run & Gun: if the modifiers drive the defense pool below 0, every 2 dice past it add 1 to the DV of the attack that hits.
SR5.NC_AucunPj: No character: the GM assigns you one.
SR5.NC_C_AideFavoris: ☆ in the list to add a favorite, ★ on a card to remove it · 12 at most · everyone has their own
SR5.NC_C_AppelerAide: The call leaves from "{appareil}" through the commcode messaging; the GM picks up for the contact. A favor is asked with the "Favor" button.
SR5.NC_C_AucunFavori: No favorite: the ☆ of a list row makes one.
SR5.NC_C_CommcodeAbsent: The system's commcode messaging cannot be found.
SR5.NC_C_DemandeRecue: {de} asks you for an introduction to {contact} (CONTACTS).
SR5.NC_C_MaDemande: Your request for an introduction to {contact}
SR5.NC_C_NoteMj:
{n} contacts in the team, {p} of them private (dashed magenta border): the GM sees them, the other players do not. The contact's owner decides the sharing.

"From" filter: a click on a name shows a single character's book.
SR5.NC_C_PasDeMj: No GM connected: the request will wait for them.
SR5.NC_C_PresentationAcceptee: Introduction accepted: {contact} ({proprietaire}'s contact) agrees to meet {de}.
SR5.NC_C_PresentationRefusee: Introduction refused by {proprietaire}: {de} will not meet {contact} that way.
SR5.NC_C_PresentationRefuseeMj: Introduction to {contact}: the contact does not follow up on {de}'s request.
SR5.NC_C_PresentationTexte: {nom} is a contact of {proprietaire}: they do not know you. {proprietaire} accepts (or not) to introduce you, then the GM decides.
SR5.NC_C_Rechercher: Search a name, a trade, a faction…
SR5.NC_C_SansCommcodeContact: This contact has no commcode and the module could not give it one.
SR5.NC_C_SansCommlink: {nom} has no device with a commcode: cannot call.
SR5.NC_C_TropDeFavoris: {nom}: you already have {n} favorites, remove one first (★ on its card).
SR5.NC_Faveurs: Favors: + the contact owes you, − you owe them
SR5.NC_JournalInaccessible: This journal is not open to you.
SR5.NC_N_AideAcces: A line adds itself when a character puts a mark on a host or enters it, or when the GM gives it. Marks = those the character still holds.
SR5.NC_N_AideBoutiques: A shop shows as soon as a character is its customer (checked on the vendor's sheet) or the GM lets it be discovered. Closed: greyed, no button.
SR5.NC_N_IndiceRepli: Rating (when the host can no longer be read)
SR5.NC_N_NoteMj: GM: {a} hidden access(es), {b} shop(s) not yet discovered.
SR5.NC_GMOnly: Only the active GM may change the Network.
SR5.NC_SettingEnabled_D: The team's book of contacts (Loyalty, Influence, favors, sharing, introductions) and the Network (matrix accesses, known shops). Two buttons in the token controls, or in the deck when the module Landing Page and Metroplexes is active. Nothing is loaded before a window opens.
SR5.NC_SettingShopsOpen_T: Network: every open shop is known
SR5.NC_SettingShopsOpen_D: Ticked, every character sees all the open shops of the world in the Network. Unticked, only those she is a client of or the GM showed her.
SR5.NC_MigrationDone: Network and Contacts: the data of the module Landing taken over by the system ({a} accesses, {c} contacts, {u} users, {r} runs with their payments).
SR5.NC_LandingLegacy: Landing Page and Metroplexes older than 1.9.0: it keeps its own copy of the Network and Contacts. Update it; meanwhile, what it adds is taken over at each load of the world.
SR5.NC_Disabled: Network and Contacts are switched off in the system settings.
SR5.NC_F_Reactions: Reacting factions (labels, no effect on reputation)
SR5.NC_F_ReactionsAide: One per line: "- Knight Errant: on edge", "+ Mafia: will like it"
SR5.NC_R_AucunMj: No run: "New run" to offer one.
SR5.NC_R_AucuneFactionRegistre: No faction in the system's registry.
SR5.NC_R_Avance: Advance (% of the pay, given when the run goes "in progress")
SR5.NC_R_AvanceAide: The run starts: the advance ({pct}% of the pay, {paie}) goes to the sheet of each character on the team, as a nuyen gain. Each line can be corrected.
SR5.NC_R_AvanceDefautAide: The value offered for a new run, changeable run by run. The book has no advance (SR5 p. 371: the employer surely did not pay up front): 0 by default.
SR5.NC_R_DejaVerse: {code}: {etape} has already been given; nothing goes out twice.
SR5.NC_R_EchoAVerser: Kept on the run, to give: {liste}.
SR5.NC_R_EchoDiffuser: Publish the echo now (otherwise: a draft to review)
SR5.NC_R_EchoNote: Linked to the run's closing: reputation {reputation} ({equipe}), {etat} in the faction registry. {versement}
SR5.NC_R_EcrireEcho: Write an echo in the news feed
SR5.NC_R_EnAttente: Pending (applied with Karma, Cutting Aces p. 157)
SR5.NC_R_MjAbsent: No GM connected: try again when they are here.
SR5.NC_R_PasDEquipe: No character on the team: nothing to give.
SR5.NC_R_PasDePersonnage: You have no character to show interest with.
SR5.NC_R_PrevusTitre: Reputation if the run succeeds (change per faction)
SR5.NC_R_PublierAide: For the whole team, or only for the ticked characters (a fixer calls someone).
SR5.NC_R_PublierPour: Publish for the ticked ones only
SR5.NC_R_RegistreAbsent: The system's faction registry is missing: nothing written.
SR5.NC_R_VersementEchec: Payment stopped on {nom}'s sheet: check their karma and nuyen history.
SR5.NC_R_VersementsTitre: Karma and nuyen for each ticked character (pay: the balance, after the advance)
SR5.NC_R_VerserMaintenant: Give it now on the sheets (otherwise: kept on the run, "Give" button in the archives)
